teamwork.1.1.1.objective: Comprehend the overall project organizational structure.
teamwork.1.1.1.task: Map out the project team's organizational chart using internal directories and create a block diagram in word and upload in the app.
teamwork.1.1.1.criterion: Accurately diagrams the reporting structure and distinct roles involved in the current project.

teamwork.1.1.2.objective: Recognize the specific duties of core technical or execution roles.
teamwork.1.1.2.task: Shadow a technical team member for a designated block of time and document their daily workflow. Write a one-page report with designation, roles and responsibilities and challenges faced within that period and upload in App.
teamwork.1.1.2.criterion: Lists key technical responsibilities and correctly explains their direct impact on project deliverables.

teamwork.1.1.3.objective: Identify the function and impact of Project Management.
teamwork.1.1.3.task: Review a current project timeline and resource allocation sheet with a Project Manager. Write a one-page report on the project, its timeline and whether sufficient resources are allotted and upload in app.
teamwork.1.1.3.criterion: Clearly explains how the Project Manager coordinates tasks and resolves bottlenecks across different departments.

teamwork.1.1.4.objective: Understand cross- functional dependencies within the team.
teamwork.1.1.4.task: Actively participate in a cross- functional stand-up or status meeting and take observational notes. Participate in two cross- functionality meeting and write a one-page report on discussion in the meeting and upload in app.
teamwork.1.1.4.criterion: Identifies and documents at least three clear dependencies between different professional roles discussed in the meeting.

teamwork.1.1.5.objective: Comprehend the role of Quality Assurance (QA) or compliance functions.
teamwork.1.1.5.task: Review recent testing reports or quality audits alongside a QA specialist. Write the feedback from the QA specialist and upload in a App.
teamwork.1.1.5.criterion: Describes how QA feedback specifically alters or guides the workflow of the design or development roles.

teamwork.1.1.6.objective: Recognize the influence of client- facing or stakeholder management roles.
teamwork.1.1.6.task: Read the initial project brief or statement of work provided by the account management team. Write a small note on the influence of the role and upload it in app.
teamwork.1.1.6.criterion: Explains how the requirements gathered by client-facing roles dictate the constraints and goals for the execution team.

teamwork.1.1.7.objective: Understand the integration of specialized support roles (e.g., IT Support, HR, Legal).
teamwork.1.1.7.task: Conduct a brief informational interview with a support staff member assigned to the project. Write the duties carried out by specialised support roles and upload it in App.
teamwork.1.1.7.criterion: Summarizes how the specialized support role enables the core project team to function efficiently and safely.

teamwork.1.1.8.objective: Analyse how different professions approach problem- solving.
teamwork.1.1.8.task: Attend a project post-mortem, retrospective, or troubleshooting session. Write a report on the problem and solving method used and upload in the App.
teamwork.1.1.8.criterion: Documents how at least two different roles approached a specific project challenge from their unique professional viewpoints.

teamwork.1.1.9.objective: Differentiate the communication priorities of various roles.
teamwork.1.1.9.task: Analyse a shared project communication channel or an extensive email thread. Analyse and email thread and write the conveyed idea in each email and upload in a App.
teamwork.1.1.9.criterion: Identifies clear variations in communication focus among different roles.

teamwork.1.1.10.objective: Synthesize individual role contributions into a cohesive whole.
teamwork.1.1.10.task: Prepare a summary presentation outlining "Who does what" for an upcoming project phase. Write the individual name and responsibilities and upload it in App.
teamwork.1.1.10.criterion: Successfully presents the summary to a supervisor, accurately detailing the interconnected contributions of at least four distinct roles.

teamwork.1.2.1.objective: Comprehend the organization's specific Diversity and Inclusion (D&I) policies.
teamwork.1.2.1.task: Review the employee handbook, corporate D&I guidelines, and complete mandatory D&I onboarding modules. Write down top three important points and upload in the app.
teamwork.1.2.1.criterion: Successfully completes onboarding assessments and accurately summarizes key workplace behavioural expectations to the supervisor.

teamwork.1.2.2.objective: Demonstrate active listening in collaborative settings.
teamwork.1.2.2.task: Participate in group meetings by allowing colleagues to finish speaking without interruption and acknowledging their points. Get feedback from the member of the meeting and upload the same to the App.
teamwork.1.2.2.criterion: Supervisor and peer feedback indicates the intern consistently listens attentively and does not talk over others.

teamwork.1.2.3.objective: Utilize inclusive language in professional communication.
teamwork.1.2.3.task: Draft internal team emails, project documentation, and chat messages using neutral, professional, and inclusive terminology. Five emails written by the candidate shall be uploaded in App.
teamwork.1.2.3.criterion: Written communications are routinely reviewed and found to be free of exclusionary, biased, or culturally insensitive language.

teamwork.1.2.4.objective: Respect differing working styles and professional backgrounds.
teamwork.1.2.4.task: Partner with a colleague from a different department or background to complete a shared project milestone. Write a note on the new ways learned from the colleague through the project.
teamwork.1.2.4.criterion: Receives positive feedback from the collaborative partner regarding the intern's adaptability, patience, and openness to alternative methods.

teamwork.1.2.5.objective: Value all team contributions equally, regardless of hierarchy.
teamwork.1.2.5.task: Co-facilitate a brainstorming session or team discussion, actively inviting input from quieter or junior members. Get feedback from the team member present on the meeting and upload in App.
teamwork.1.2.5.criterion: Successfully elicits and respectfully documents input from all meeting attendees, ensuring no single voice dominates the session.

teamwork.1.2.6.task: Review provided internal training materials, webinars, or articles on workplace sensitivity and unconscious bias. Write three important points and upload in App.
teamwork.1.2.6.criterion: Can accurately identify examples of non-inclusive behaviour in hypothetical scenarios and articulate strategies to maintain a respectful environment.

teamwork.1.2.7.objective: Navigate professional disagreements with tact and respect.
teamwork.1.2.7.task: Engage in a project design or strategy review, ensuring all critiques are focused strictly on the work/ideas and not the individual. Analyse a similar scenario and include your thoughts on how it can be approached and upload it in App.
teamwork.1.2.7.criterion: Maintains a calm, objective tone during debates and reaches compromises without escalating to personal conflict.

teamwork.1.2.8.objective: Respect colleagues' time, schedules, and professional boundaries.
teamwork.1.2.8.task: Organize project check-ins using shared calendars, strictly observing colleagues' working hours, time zones, and "focus time" blocks. Write a note on the experience of organising a meeting with colleagues and upload it in App.
teamwork.1.2.8.criterion: 100% of meetings scheduled by the intern respect calendar availability and begin/end precisely on time.

teamwork.1.2.9.objective: Support accessibility standards in shared workspaces and outputs.
teamwork.1.2.9.task: Create or format shared team documents and presentations ensuring basic accessibility. Upload the presentation in App
teamwork.1.2.9.criterion: Materials submitted by the intern pass a baseline accessibility check and can be easily utilized by all team members.

teamwork.1.2.10.objective: Contribute to a psychologically safe and welcoming team culture.
teamwork.1.2.10.task: Actively participate in team-building activities, check-ins, or introductions, extending a welcoming demeanour to all peers. Take feedback from team members about the participation and upload in App
teamwork.1.2.10.criterion: End-of-rotation peer evaluations specifically highlight the intern's approachable demeanour and positive contribution to team morale.

teamwork.2.1.1.objective: Comprehend the specific requirements and parameters of an assigned task.
teamwork.2.1.1.task: Review the assignment brief and ask clarifying questions to the supervisor. Write a small note on the assignment and upload in App
teamwork.2.1.1.criterion: Can accurately restate the task goals, required deliverables, and deadlines back to the supervisor.

teamwork.2.1.2.objective: Manage individual time effectively to meet shared project deadlines.
teamwork.2.1.2.task: Create a personal timeline or checklist to track daily progress on the assigned project. Write down the check list on the App
teamwork.2.1.2.criterion: Consistently submits interim drafts or status updates according to the schedule agreed upon with the supervisor.

teamwork.2.1.3.objective: Execute tasks according to established team standards.
teamwork.2.1.3.task: Follow a specific standard operating procedure to complete a task. Write the steps of execution and upload in the App
teamwork.2.1.3.criterion: The final output adheres strictly to provided technical or formatting guidelines, requiring minimal structural corrections.

teamwork.2.1.4.task: Identify when a task is stalled due to missing information or technical issues and immediately notify the supervisor. Involve in a project and note down the roadblock faced and upload in App.
teamwork.2.1.4.criterion: Escalates issues promptly rather than hiding delays, providing a clear summary of what is needed to proceed.

teamwork.2.1.5.objective: Perform basic quality control on individual deliverables.
teamwork.2.1.5.task: Conduct a self-review of the completed portion before submitting it for review. Write a note about the self-review and upload it in the App
teamwork.2.1.5.criterion: Submitted work demonstrates high attention to detail and accurately addresses all baseline requirements outlined in the initial brief.

teamwork.2.1.6.objective: Navigate project hand-offs and shared workspaces.
teamwork.2.1.6.task: Upload, format, or merge the completed assigned portion into the team's designated drive. Upload the screen shot in the App.
teamwork.2.1.6.criterion: Files and deliverables are correctly named, properly organized, and easily accessible to the rest of the team.

teamwork.2.1.7.objective: Receive and implement constructive feedback effectively.
teamwork.2.1.7.task: Review the supervisors redlines or feedback on an initial draft and execute the requested revisions. Write note on the understanding of feedback from supervisor and upload it in App.
teamwork.2.1.7.criterion: The second iteration of the work accurately incorporates all supervisory feedback without needing repeated corrections on the same issues.

teamwork.2.1.8.objective: Understand the impact of individual delays on team dependencies.
teamwork.2.1.8.task: Map out how their specific assigned task feeds into the next phase of a colleague's workflow. Create a chart with input and output from each team and upload it in App.
teamwork.2.1.8.criterion: Accurately identifies which team member is waiting on their deliverable and explains why timely completion is critical to the broader project.

teamwork.2.1.9.objective: Demonstrate reliability in meeting final delivery expectations.
teamwork.2.1.9.task: Commit to and deliver the finalized portion of a collaborative project phase by the deadline. Write the experience about the final deliverable (challenges faced and overcame) and upload in App
teamwork.2.1.9.criterion: Delivers the completed, review-ready task on or before the deadline 100% of the time or negotiates an extension with the supervisor well in advance.

teamwork.2.1.10.objective: Close out tasks using proper reporting protocols.
teamwork.2.1.10.task: Formally conclude the assignment by updating the status in the project tracker and notifying relevant stakeholders. Upload the Screenshot of the tracker and email notification in the App.
teamwork.2.1.10.criterion: tools reflect the accurate "completed" status, and the supervisor is explicitly notified that the hand-off is ready.

teamwork.2.2.1.objective: Accurately assess the completion and quality of primary assignments.
teamwork.2.2.1.task: Complete a self-review of assigned deliverables and obtain supervisor sign-off before seeking additional work. Write a note about review and upload in App
teamwork.2.2.1.criterion: Supervisor confirms that the intern's primary tasks are 100% complete and meet quality standards before the intern initiates help elsewhere.

teamwork.2.2.2.objective: Develop situational awareness regarding the team's overall workload.
teamwork.2.2.2.task: Review the team's project management board (e.g., Kanban, Jira) daily to identify backlogged items or colleagues with heavy task loads. Write a note on the backlog and overload team member for the particular week and upload in App
teamwork.2.2.2.criterion: Can accurately point out at least two areas where the team is currently facing resource constraints or approaching tight deadlines.

teamwork.2.2.3.objective: Proactively communicate availability to the team.
teamwork.2.2.3.task: Send a concise, professional message to the team channel or supervisor stating current availability and offering specific support. Upload the screenshot of the message and upload in App
teamwork.2.2.3.criterion: Communications offering help are timely, polite, and clearly state the intern's current capacity without sounding demanding.

teamwork.2.2.4.objective: Assess personal capabilities to offer relevant assistance.
teamwork.2.2.4.task: Match personal skills to the specific needs of a struggling team member. Write note about the personal skill present, how it was used and upload in App
teamwork.2.2.4.criterion: Offers help on tasks where they possess the necessary baseline competence, avoiding taking on highly specialized tasks beyond their current capability.

teamwork.2.2.5.objective: Clarify the scope and expectations of secondary tasks.
teamwork.2.2.5.task: Conduct a brief alignment check with the colleague receiving help to understand the exact requirements and deadline of the delegated work. Write a note about the goal, timeframe and expected output and upload in App.
teamwork.2.2.5.criterion: Can accurately summarize the goal, timeframe, and expected output format of the assisting task before initiating the work.

teamwork.2.2.6.objective: Adapt to colleagues' preferred workflows and tools.
teamwork.2.2.6.task: Complete a support task utilizing the specific file structures, naming conventions, or software preferred by the colleague being helped. Get a feedback from the colleague about the integration into the project and upload in App.
teamwork.2.2.6.criterion: The assisted colleague reports that the intern seamlessly integrated into their process without causing disruption or requiring excessive handholding.

teamwork.2.2.7.objective: Differentiate and track time spent on support tasks.
teamwork.2.2.7.task: Log time spent assisting others separately from primary tasks in the team's time-tracking software or daily report. Take a screenshot of the time log spent on support activities and upload in App
teamwork.2.2.7.criterion: Time logs show a clear, accurate distinction between core duties and support duties.

teamwork.2.2.8.objective: Provide support with a constructive and positive demeanour.
teamwork.2.2.8.task: Assist a peer with a repetitive, foundational, or menial task to help them meet a critical project milestone. Collect feedback from peers and upload in App
teamwork.2.2.8.criterion: Peer feedback highlights the intern's willingness to help with foundational tasks without complaint and with a collaborative attitude.

teamwork.2.2.9.objective: Recognize professional boundaries and focus time.
teamwork.2.2.9.task: Observe colleagues' status indicators and refrain from interrupting deep focus work to offer help. Collect feedback from colleague about the assistance offered and upload in App.
teamwork.2.2.9.criterion: Consistently respects colleagues' focus time and only offers assistance during appropriate break points, open communication windows, or via asynchronous channels.

teamwork.2.2.10.objective: Document shared efforts for seamless hand- backs.
teamwork.2.2.10.task: Write a brief handover summary or leave clear comments detailing the steps taken and progress made on the assisted task. Upload the summary in App.
teamwork.2.2.10.criterion: The primary task owner can immediately resume the work based on the clarity and completeness of the intern's documentation and handover notes.

teamwork.3.1.1.objective: Demonstrate openness and active listening when receiving peer feedback.
teamwork.3.1.1.task: Participate in a peer-review session or 1-on-1 critique of a draft, taking detailed notes without interrupting the reviewer. Collect feedback from peers about the active listening and upload in App
teamwork.3.1.1.criterion: Supervisor or peer confirms the intern listened attentively, asked clarifying questions, and did not exhibit defensive behaviour.

teamwork.3.1.2.objective: Accurately interpret and document provided feedback.
teamwork.3.1.2.task: Restate or summarize the verbal feedback received in a follow-up email or comment thread to ensure total alignment. Upload the summarised verbal feedback in App
teamwork.3.1.2.criterion: The written summary accurately reflects the reviewer's original intent without omitting or misinterpreting critical points.

teamwork.3.1.3.objective: Differentiate between mandatory corrections and subjective suggestions.
teamwork.3.1.3.task: Review a list of peer comments and categorize them into "required technical fixes" versus "stylistic recommendations." Upload the categorised comments in the App
teamwork.3.1.3.criterion: Accurately prioritizes the feedback, ensuring all factual, structural, or compliance errors are marked as mandatory fixes.

teamwork.3.1.4.objective: Translate vague feedback into actionable steps.
teamwork.3.1.4.task: Identify an ambiguous comment and ask the reviewer targeted questions to define exactly what needs changing. Note the ambiguous comment and write down the explanation provided by the colleague and upload in App
teamwork.3.1.4.criterion: Successfully turns a general critique into a concrete, executable task through professional and polite follow-up communication.

teamwork.3.1.5.objective: Execute specific technical or formatting revisions accurately.
teamwork.3.1.5.task: Revise a submitted draft, calculation, or code snippet to directly incorporate the specific redlines provided by a senior team member. Get feedback about the draft and upload in App.
teamwork.3.1.5.criterion: The subsequent version of the work product includes 100% of the agreed-upon corrections, accurately executed.

teamwork.3.1.6.objective: Resolve conflicting feedback from multiple stakeholders.
teamwork.3.1.6.task: Identify contradictory comments from two different team members on a shared document and facilitate a brief alignment chat to find a resolution. In a document include both the comments and explain the conflicts and resolution and upload in App.
teamwork.3.1.6.criterion: Successfully navigates the conflict with tact, producing a final output that satisfies the core project requirements of both parties.

teamwork.3.1.7.objective: Utilize version control and change tracking effectively.
teamwork.3.1.7.task: Implement requested revisions using "Track Changes," version control commit messages, or by maintaining a clear change log. Upload Screen shot of the log in the App.
teamwork.3.1.7.criterion: The change log or tracked document clearly and explicitly maps the executed revisions back to the specific feedback received.

teamwork.3.1.8.objective: Verify the successful integration of feedback (Closing the Loop).
teamwork.3.1.8.task: Resubmit the revised work to the original reviewer, explicitly highlighting where and how their concerns were addressed. Take a note of the concerns and solution and upload in App.
teamwork.3.1.8.criterion: The reviewer signs off on the revised deliverable without needing to repeat or re-explain their initial feedback.

teamwork.3.1.9.objective: Generalize feedback to prevent repeating past mistakes.
teamwork.3.1.9.task: Create a personal "quality assurance checklist" based on previous feedback and use it to self-review a brand-new assignment. Create the checklist and note the feedback based on the checklist and upload in App.
teamwork.3.1.9.criterion: The new assignment demonstrates that the intern has internalized past lessons, entirely avoiding the errors corrected in previous review cycles.

teamwork.3.1.10.objective: Maintain a professional and appreciative demeanour throughout the review cycle.
teamwork.3.1.10.task: Thank the reviewer for their time and constructive insights once the final deliverable is approved. Take screen shot of the replies and upload in App.
teamwork.3.1.10.criterion: Consistently demonstrates professionalism and gratitude, visibly treating the feedback loop as a collaborative growth opportunity rather than a personal critique.

teamwork.3.2.1.objective: Differentiate between credible, high-value resources and general noise.
teamwork.3.2.1.task: Curate a short list of industry articles, software tools, or tutorials that are highly relevant to the team's current project phase. Note the list a document and upload in App.
teamwork.3.2.1.criterion: Supervisor confirms the selected resources are accurate, up-to-date, and from reputable, industry- standard sources.

teamwork.3.2.2.objective: Identify knowledge gaps or technical bottlenecks within the team.
teamwork.3.2.2.task: Monitor team discussions or stand-up meetings to pinpoint recurring questions or workflow inefficiencies. Take a note of the workflow inefficiencies, recurring questions and upload in App.
teamwork.3.2.2.criterion: Accurately identifies at least one specific technical area where the team could directly benefit from supplementary information.

teamwork.3.2.3.objective: Utilize appropriate internal communication channels for knowledge sharing.
teamwork.3.2.3.task: Post a relevant technical insight or resource link in the team's designated knowledge-sharing forum. Take a screenshot of the post and upload in App.
teamwork.3.2.3.criterion: The resource is shared in the correct, centralized forum rather than being lost in direct messages or fragmented emails.

teamwork.3.2.4.objective: Provide clear context and actionable takeaways for shared information.
teamwork.3.2.4.task: Write a brief, scannable summary accompanying a shared link, explicitly explaining why it is useful and how it applies to the project. Upload the summary in App
teamwork.3.2.4.criterion: Colleagues can instantly understand the relevance and value of the resource from the summary without having to read the entire source first.

teamwork.3.2.5.objective: Translate personal problem-solving breakthroughs into shared knowledge.
teamwork.3.2.5.task: Write a brief "how-to" snippet or mini-SOP after successfully navigating a new technical challenge or software quirk. Upload the same in App.
teamwork.3.2.5.criterion: The written snippet is clear, easily reproducible by peers, and successfully added to the team's shared documentation repository.

teamwork.3.2.6.objective: Articulate technical insights verbally in an accessible manner.
teamwork.3.2.6.task: Prepare and deliver a brief informal demo showing a newly discovered software shortcut, technique, or best practice. Photos or videos of the demo to be uploaded in App.
teamwork.3.2.6.criterion: The presentation is concise, avoids unnecessary jargon, and peers confirm they learned a usable new skill.

teamwork.3.2.7.objective: Update and maintain the accuracy of existing team knowledge bases.
teamwork.3.2.7.task: Proactively review an existing shared team document, identify an outdated process or broken link, and update it with current information. Write e note about the damage and repair and upload in App.
teamwork.3.2.7.criterion: The updated document is technically sound, functional, and the intern successfully notifies the team of the revision.

teamwork.3.2.8.objective: Tailor insights to the specific needs of different roles.
teamwork.3.2.8.task: Direct a highly specialized technical article or tool directly to a specific colleague whose role aligns perfectly with the content. Create the combination and provide explanation of the suitability and upload in App.
teamwork.3.2.8.criterion: The recipient confirms the shared resource is highly relevant and immediately applicable to their specific tasks.

teamwork.3.2.9.task: Ask a targeted, open-ended question in a team forum requesting peers to share their favourite approaches or tools for a specific task. Take a screen shot of the questions and response and upload in App.
teamwork.3.2.9.criterion: Successfully initiates a constructive technical discussion that prompts at least two other colleagues to share their own insights.

teamwork.3.2.10.objective: Establish a consistent habit of continuous sharing.
teamwork.3.2.10.task: Commit to sharing at least one highly relevant technical insight, workflow improvement, or resource per project phase or sprint. Write a note on the suggestions provided and explanations and upload in App.
teamwork.3.2.10.criterion: End-of-rotation evaluations indicate the intern established a reliable pattern of contribution, rather than treating knowledge sharing as a one-off event.

teamwork.4.1.1.objective: Identify the objective root cause of a technical or interpersonal disagreement.
teamwork.4.1.1.task: Observe a minor team disagreement and write down the core conflicting points objectively. Take a note of the conflicting point and reason for disagreement and ways to resolve it and upload in App.
teamwork.4.1.1.criterion: Accurately isolates the core issue (e.g., conflicting requirements, missing data) without assigning personal blame or bias.

teamwork.4.1.2.objective: Apply active de- escalation techniques during tense discussions.
teamwork.4.1.2.task: Intervene in a stalling technical debate by suggesting a brief pause or restating the shared project goal. Feedback from a member of the meeting shall be collected and upload in App.
teamwork.4.1.2.criterion: Successfully lowers the emotional temperature of the discussion, refocusing the team on the objective deliverable.

teamwork.4.1.3.objective: Utilize authoritative project documentation to resolve technical ambiguities.
teamwork.4.1.3.task: Retrieve the original project brief, SOP, or technical manual to clarify a disputed requirement during a meeting. Write a note about the experience of solving it and upload in App.
teamwork.4.1.3.criterion: Resolves the misalignment quickly by referencing factual, approved documentation rather than relying on opinions.

teamwork.4.1.4.objective: Validate differing perspectives to foster a collaborative resolution environment.
teamwork.4.1.4.task: Verbally summarize each party's viewpoint during a disagreement before suggesting a path forward. Write a note on the summary and upload in App.
teamwork.4.1.4.criterion: Both conflicting parties explicitly confirm the intern accurately and fairly represented their individual perspectives.

teamwork.4.1.5.objective: Propose actionable compromises for conflicting technical approaches.
teamwork.4.1.5.task: Draft a hybrid solution or middle- ground proposal when two peers disagree on a workflow step. Write a note on the disagreement and solution proposed and upload in App.
teamwork.4.1.5.criterion: Proposes a logical compromise that addresses the primary concerns of both parties while strictly aligning with project constraints.

teamwork.4.1.6.objective: Differentiate between minor misalignments and conflicts requiring escalation.
teamwork.4.1.6.task: Evaluate a current conflict against an escalation matrix or established team protocols to determine the next step. Write differentiated escalation and upload in App.
teamwork.4.1.6.criterion: Correctly identifies whether to mediate the issue locally or escalate it to the supervisor based on the conflict's impact on budget, scope, or safety.

teamwork.4.1.7.objective: Guide a deadlocked team towards a consensus decision.
teamwork.4.1.7.task: Facilitate a brief, structured pros-and- cons analysis on a whiteboard for two competing technical options. Take a photo or screenshot of the pros and cons and upload in App.
teamwork.4.1.7.criterion: Guides the involved team members to a unified decision, ensuring all parties agree to commit to the chosen path.

teamwork.4.1.8.objective: Maintain strict neutrality and avoid taking sides in peer disputes.
teamwork.4.1.8.task: Act as an impartial sounding board during a minor disagreement between two colleagues. Collect feedback from a third person involved in the meeting and upload in App.
teamwork.4.1.8.criterion: Peer and supervisor feedback confirms the intern acted fairly, without expressing personal favouritism or bias toward either party.

teamwork.4.1.9.objective: Document resolutions to prevent recurring misalignments.
teamwork.4.1.9.task: Write a summary of the agreed-upon technical approach after a conflict is resolved and share it in the team channel. Upload the summary in App.
teamwork.4.1.9.criterion: The documented resolution is clear, technically accurate, and formally acknowledged by all involved parties.

teamwork.4.1.10.objective: Re-establish rapport and positive team dynamics after a disagreement.
teamwork.4.1.10.task: Initiate a positive, forward-looking interaction or offer specific task assistance to the involved parties after a conflict is closed. collect evidence about the re-establishment using feedback or scripture and upload in App.
teamwork.4.1.10.criterion: Demonstrates no lingering tension and successfully restores a normal, collaborative working rhythm with the peers involved.

teamwork.4.2.1.objective: Assess the baseline knowledge of a peer before providing guidance.
teamwork.4.2.1.task: Conduct a brief introductory conversation with a new team member to gauge their familiarity with a specific project tool or workflow. Rate their familiarity with a specific tool on the App.
teamwork.4.2.1.criterion: Accurately identifies the peer's knowledge gaps and tailors the subsequent explanation to match their specific experience level.

teamwork.4.2.2.objective: Translate complex technical concepts into accessible language.
teamwork.4.2.2.task: Explain a core project methodology or technical requirement to a junior peer using clear analogies and avoiding unnecessary jargon. Create a small presentation of any topic and explain it to a junior and upload the presentation in App.
teamwork.4.2.2.criterion: The guided peer can accurately reiterate the core concept in their own words without relying on the original technical jargon.

teamwork.4.2.3.task: Perform a shadowing session where the intern executes a task while narrating the steps, then observes the newer peer attempting the same task. Write a report on the steps used by both parties and upload in App.
teamwork.4.2.3.criterion: The new peer successfully replicates the task, with the intern providing immediate, constructive, and patient corrections when errors occur.

teamwork.4.2.4.objective: Develop asynchronous support materials for peer learning.
teamwork.4.2.4.task: Create a simple one-page "quick start guide" or a visual checklist for a routine team task to serve as a reference tool. Upload the quick start guide on App.
teamwork.4.2.4.criterion: The created guide is clear, visually organized, technically accurate, and enables a new peer to complete the task independently.

teamwork.4.2.5.objective: Foster a psychologically safe environment for questions
teamwork.4.2.5.task: Dedicate specific time during a joint assignment for a Q&A session, explicitly encouraging the newer member to voice any uncertainties. Take photos or videos of the Q&A session and upload in App.
teamwork.4.2.5.criterion: Feedback from the mentored peer highlights the intern's patience, approachability, and non-judgmental demeanor when answering fundamental questions.

teamwork.4.2.6.objective: Provide guidance while preserving peer autonomy.
teamwork.4.2.6.task: Assign a manageable sub-task to a newer peer, provide initial context, and step back, offering support only when explicitly requested. Collect feedback about the availability from new peers and upload in App.
teamwork.4.2.6.criterion: Strikes a successful balance between being available for support and allowing the peer to struggle constructively to find the solution without micromanagement.

teamwork.4.2.7.objective: Deliver constructive and actionable feedback on peer work
teamwork.4.2.7.task: Review a draft completed by a newer peer and provide specific, supportive, and actionable suggestions for improvement. Make a note of all the feedback suggested, made and upload in App.
teamwork.4.2.7.criterion: Feedback is framed positively, focuses on the work rather than the individual, and provides concrete, step-by-step guidance for improvement.

problem_solving.1.1.1.objective: To identify the main technical problems encountered in the given tasks.
problem_solving.1.1.1.task: Spotting visible technical errors in operational tasks performed in virtually rendered 3D environments or videos.
problem_solving.1.1.1.criterion: Successfully indentifies visible technical errors in a virtual environment (3D/video) by clicking on the correct points within the time limit.

problem_solving.1.1.2.objective: To identify fundamental deviations from the expected operating conditions of a system, product, or process.
problem_solving.1.1.2.task: Identify deviations by matching the virtual system's operational data displayed on the screen with standard reference values using a "drag-and-drop" method.
problem_solving.1.1.2.criterion: Groups the operational data of the virtual system displayed on the screen correctly using the "drag- and-drop" method without incorrect matching.

problem_solving.1.1.3.objective: To express the problem by observing the symptoms of technical issues.
problem_solving.1.1.3.task: By examining the encountered physical symptoms or error messages, select the correct technical terms from the in-app menu to identify the problem.
problem_solving.1.1.3.criterion: Accurately describes the problem with 100% precision by selecting the most appropriate technical terms from an interactive menu based on the symptoms or error messages encountered.

problem_solving.1.1.4.objective: To collect basic, surface-level data and observation results related to the problem.
problem_solving.1.1.4.task: Collecting measurement data, images, and user feedback from virtual devices in the application interface and transferring them to a digital dashboard.
problem_solving.1.1.4.criterion: Collects all required measurement data and visuals from virtual devices without skipping anything and transfers them completely to the in-game digital scoreboard.

problem_solving.1.1.5.objective: To identify potential technical issues by reviewing the requirements of assigned tasks.
problem_solving.1.1.5.task: In the app, identify potential problem areas and risk points in job descriptions and workflows by marking them with an interactive highlighter.
problem_solving.1.1.5.criterion: Highlights all potential risk areas in the workflows within the scenario in a comprehensive and interconnected manner using an interactive pen.

problem_solving.1.1.6.objective: To identify the scope of the technical issues encountered and the components affected.
problem_solving.1.1.6.task: Mapping the area affected by the technical issue by selecting each piece of equipment, module, and component individually on the interactive system diagram in the app.
problem_solving.1.1.6.criterion: Accurately and clearly maps all components affected by the technical problem on an interactive diagram, eliminating the need for incorrect part selection.

problem_solving.1.1.7.objective: To identify simple, superficial technical errors, deficiencies, or irregularities.
problem_solving.1.1.7.task: Performing visual inspections on virtual equipment to identify and label superficial errors and deficiencies.
problem_solving.1.1.7.criterion: During a virtual visual inspection, identifies all surface defects and physical deficiencies without missing and labels them with the correct names.

problem_solving.1.1.8.objective: To make a preliminary assessment of the source of technical problems and listing possible causes.
problem_solving.1.1.8.task: Based on observation results for various technical problem scenarios presented in the application, drag and drop logical causes from a pool of possible solutions to create a preliminary evaluation list.
problem_solving.1.1.8.criterion: Accurately selects possible causes from the pool that logically match the observational data, creating a complete preliminary assessment list.

problem_solving.1.1.9.objective: To record any technical issues identified using appropriate tools such as checklists, trouble tickets, and reports.
problem_solving.1.1.9.task: Reporting issues to the system by filling out the digital trouble ticket form and checklists within the application.
problem_solving.1.1.9.criterion: Completes all required fields on the digital trouble ticket and checklists with accurate technical information and approves the form.

problem_solving.1.1.10.objective: To perform the necessary basic checks to confirm the presence of technical issues.
problem_solving.1.1.10.task: Confirm or deny the presence of a problem by simulating the basic checks specified in the procedure using virtual measurement tools.
problem_solving.1.1.10.criterion: To confirm the problem, simulates the essential checks required, using virtual measurement tools and strictly following the standard procedure.

problem_solving.1.2.1.objective: To describe the basic steps engineers follow when identifying a technical problem.
problem_solving.1.2.1.task: A puzzle to arrange event cards, which illustrate an engineer's problem definition process, such as data collection, testing, etc., in chronological order.
problem_solving.1.2.1.criterion: Arranges the event cards, which illustrate the problem definition steps, in a logical and chronologically perfect order on the first attempt.

problem_solving.1.2.2.objective: To describe the observation methods used in the process of identifying a problem.
problem_solving.1.2.2.task: A mini game that matches various observation scenarios, such as field inspections and performance monitoring, with the correct observation method names.
problem_solving.1.2.2.criterion: Completes various observation scenarios with the corresponding observation method names (for example field inspection, etc.) without mismatching.

problem_solving.1.2.3.objective: To list the types of data engineers collect for the purpose of problem identification.
problem_solving.1.2.3.task: Separate the displayed sensor data, log records, and feedback into the appropriate data type folders, such as qualitative/quantitative, etc. by dragging and dropping.
problem_solving.1.2.3.criterion: Correctly classifies different data types as qualitative/quantitative, etc. displayed on the screen by accurately shifting them to their respective folders within a time constraint.

problem_solving.1.2.4.objective: To describe the measurement, testing, and inspection activities used in identifying technical problems.
problem_solving.1.2.4.task: The measurement and testing simulations are conducted in a virtual environment, and in- game flashcards are used to answer questions about the purpose of each.
problem_solving.1.2.4.criterion: After virtual test simulations, provides technically correct answers to the objective or scope questions presented on the flashcards.

problem_solving.1.2.5.objective: To describe the fundamental questions and inquiry techniques engineers use when defining a problem.
problem_solving.1.2.5.task: In a problem scenario, select the most appropriate inquiry technique or question from an interactive dialogue tree to find the root cause.
problem_solving.1.2.5.criterion: In the interactive dialogue tree, the most accurate inquiry route to finding the root cause, rather than focusing on superficial symptoms, is found in a logical flow.

problem_solving.1.2.6.objective: To understand the process by which engineers distinguish between the symptoms and root causes of a technical problem.
problem_solving.1.2.6.task: Separate the mixed fault conditions by swiping them into "Symptom" or "Root Cause" boxes.
problem_solving.1.2.6.criterion: Separates whether the information on the fault cards it encounters is a "Symptom" or a "Root Cause" by swiping it into boxes with 100% accuracy.

problem_solving.1.2.7.objective: To describe the documentation and record-keeping methods engineers use during the problem identification process.
problem_solving.1.2.7.task: Documenting the process by correctly matching the appropriate documentation format, such as failure report, maintenance log, etc. for a case study in a virtual environment.
problem_solving.1.2.7.criterion: Correctly selects and matches the most appropriate documentation format, such as failure report, maintenance log, etc. that meets the technical requirements of the given case scenario.

problem_solving.1.2.8.objective: To identify common elements in problem- identification approaches applied to different technical problems.
problem_solving.1.2.8.task: Identify common diagnostic steps in different technical failure cases and combine them on an interactive Venn diagram.
problem_solving.1.2.8.criterion: By analysing the steps of different failure cases, it accurately places the intersecting common diagnostic steps at the center of the interactive Venn diagram.

problem_solving.1.2.9.objective: To observe the problem- identification process conducted by an engineer and list its stages.
problem_solving.1.2.9.task: While watching a short video of a virtual process, pause the screen at critical stages and record the steps of the process in a timeline.
problem_solving.1.2.9.criterion: In the virtual process it monitors, pauses the video precisely at the critical breaking points where the engineer takes action, recording the process step by step in a time tunnel.

problem_solving.1.2.10.objective: To describe the observed problem- identification process verbally or in writing using technical terminology.
problem_solving.1.2.10.task: Drag and drop the appropriate terms from the in-app technical vocabulary pool to fill in the blanks in the summary text of the observed process.
problem_solving.1.2.10.criterion: Accurately fills in the gaps in the summary text of the observed process using correct words selected from a pool of technical terminology.

problem_solving.2.1.1.objective: To understand the fault diagnosis plan and methodological steps to be followed for engineering problems.
problem_solving.2.1.1.task: Set a logical workflow diagram by dragging and dropping the complex diagnostic steps as troubleshooting roadmap provided under mentor guidance.
problem_solving.2.1.1.criterion: Places the mixed diagnostic steps provided by the mentor into the diagram in their complete and correct order, in accordance with the system's logical workflow rules.

problem_solving.2.1.2.objective: To collecting and present the required technical data for specific fault types or anomalies within the scope of engineering problems.
problem_solving.2.1.2.task: Systematically extract critical parameters, such as temperature, pressure from virtual device screens and enter them into a digital reporting table.
problem_solving.2.1.2.criterion: Reads all critical parameters, such as temperature, pressure, etc. displayed on the virtual device screens without missing and records the correct values in the digital reporting table.

problem_solving.2.1.3.objective: To use basic engineering fault diagnosis and testing tools safely and accurately as required.
problem_solving.2.1.3.task: Reading and recording error codes using diagnostic simulations such as virtual multimeters and oscilloscopes, while adhering to occupational safety and health (OSH) rules.
problem_solving.2.1.3.criterion: By using virtual testing devices in accordance with occupational safety and health (OSH) rules, in the correct sequence and with the correct calibration settings, it accurately detects error codes.

problem_solving.2.1.4.objective: To compare engineering problem symptoms with technical documentation and reference values.
problem_solving.2.1.4.task: Review the P&IDs and electrical schematics (CAD) in the application to identify and mark any deviations between physical failure indicators and reference values.
problem_solving.2.1.4.criterion: By reviewing the P&IDs and electrical schematics (CAD) in the system, accurately identifies and clearly marks any deviations between physical fault indicators and reference values.

problem_solving.2.1.5.objective: To contribute structured ideas to ongoing Root Cause Analysis (RCA) processes under mentor guidance.
problem_solving.2.1.5.task: Fill in the missing causal branches in the interactive fishbone (Ishikawa) pattern, opened with the guidance of the mentor in the application, using the technical tips provided.
problem_solving.2.1.5.criterion: Fills in the blank cause-and- effect branches in the interactive fishbone diagram with correct arguments by logically analysing the technical clues in the system.

problem_solving.2.1.6.objective: To perform validation experiments or tests conducted by the mentor to identify the source of the problem.
problem_solving.2.1.6.task: Perform functional tests by preserving or modifying the virtual parameters defined by the mentor, and record any changes made to the interface in real time.
problem_solving.2.1.6.criterion: Manipulates the virtual parameters in full accordance with the mentor's testing instructions and records the system's real-time reactions to the interface with zero latency.

problem_solving.2.1.7.objective: To record the steps taken and interim findings in the diagnostic process using technical language.
problem_solving.2.1.7.task: Adding each intervention in the fault diagnosis process or simulation to the technical logbook chronologically with a timestamp.
problem_solving.2.1.7.criterion: Records all technical interventions in the fault diagnosis simulation in the digital logbook, without omitting any, along with the correct timestamps and engineering terminology.

problem_solving.2.1.8.objective: To observe the distinction between systemic/structural failures and normal operational wear and tear and contributing to the diagnostic process.
problem_solving.2.1.8.task: Compare the visual examples and indicate whether the condition constitutes “Acceptable Wear and Tear” or “Systematic Error”.
problem_solving.2.1.8.criterion: By analysing images of damaged/worn parts, it assigns "Acceptable Wear" and "Systematic Error" labels to the correct cases with 100% accuracy.

problem_solving.2.1.9.objective: To visualize diagnostic data for technical reporting and presentations.
problem_solving.2.1.9.task: Create interactive trend curves and graphs with adjusted axes and tolerances using the raw test data provided by the application. Upload these to the system.

problem_solving.2.1.10.objective: To supporting final reporting and decision- making processes towards definitive diagnosis.

problem_solving.2.2.1.objective: To understand accepted troubleshooting procedures and standard operating guidelines for simple technical problems.

problem_solving.2.2.2.objective: To prepare the necessary technical materials, components, and equipment for solving simple technical problems.

problem_solving.2.2.3.objective: To perform standard repair or part replacement procedures under supervision.

problem_solving.2.2.4.objective: To apply standard calibration and adjustment procedures on systems or products.

problem_solving.2.2.5.objective: To report unexpected intermediate technical challenges encountered during solution implementation.

problem_solving.2.2.6.objective: To apply standard test procedures to verify the effectiveness of the implemented solution.

problem_solving.2.2.7.objective: To compare and schematizing post- solution performance data with design reference values.

problem_solving.2.2.8.objective: To document the steps and changes of the implemented technical solution in a professional format.

problem_solving.2.2.8.criterion: Records the serial numbers of newly integrated components and the final verification results completely and permanently in the digital maintenance database without formatting errors.

problem_solving.2.2.9.objective: To provide standard preventive maintenance recommendations to ensure the longevity of the solution.
problem_solving.2.2.9.task: Drag and drop preventative maintenance recommendations, such as cleaning or calibration routines, into the system to prevent recurrence of the problem.
problem_solving.2.2.9.criterion: To prevent the problem from recurring, integrates the most appropriate preventive maintenance recommendations such as lubrication, cleaning, etc. into the system, drawing them from a pool of recommendations to extend the system's lifespan.

problem_solving.2.2.10.objective: To support the completion of the solution process and system commissioning activities.
problem_solving.2.2.10.task: Approving the interim tasks assigned during system commissioning and digitally signing the handover form to the operations team. Uploading this form to the system.
problem_solving.2.2.10.criterion: By fully completing all safety and control sub-tasks in the system commissioning scenario, the user successfully approves the digital handover form and uploads it to the system.

problem_solving.3.1.1.objective: To independently define an encountered engineering problem, including its scope, boundary conditions, technical requirements, and expected outcomes.
problem_solving.3.1.1.task: Taking character limits into account, describe the boundary conditions, constraints, and expected results of a virtual problem scenario in an interactive “Problem Definition Document.”
problem_solving.3.1.1.criterion: Formulates the boundary conditions, technical constraints, and outputs of the simulation scenario as a complete summary, in accordance with technical terminology and within the character limits of the “Problem Definition Document”

problem_solving.3.1.2.objective: To identify the necessary technical data for the problem, collect it from appropriate sources, and prepare it for analysis.
problem_solving.3.1.2.task: Combining relevant data from different digital databases, including historical maintenance logs and sensor data, into a single analysis workspace.
problem_solving.3.1.2.criterion: Retrieves the necessary sensor and maintenance log data for diagnosis from multiple digital databases with zero loss and combines them into a single, cleaned dataset pool ready for analysis.

problem_solving.3.1.3.objective: To evaluate the accuracy, reliability, and suitability of the collected data from an engineering perspective.
problem_solving.3.1.3.task: Filter calibration errors, outliers, and missing data on the dataset by clicking through an interactive chart.
problem_solving.3.1.3.criterion: Finds and clicks on all manipulated calibration errors and statistical outliers in the data graph, bringing the dataset to 100% accuracy.

problem_solving.3.1.4.objective: To use methods such as observation, measurement, comparison, cause-and- effect analysis, or root cause analysis to identify the root causes of the problem.
problem_solving.3.1.4.task: Fill in a blank "Fishbone" diagram or "5 Whys" table with interactive blocks to identify root causes through independent analysis.
problem_solving.3.1.4.criterion: To get past the superficial symptoms of the problem and find the root cause, constructs Fishbone blocks flawlessly with logical arguments that perfectly fit the causal link.

problem_solving.3.1.5.objective: To quantitatively analyse the effects of the problem using field data, measurement results, production records, maintenance history, or performance indicators.
problem_solving.3.1.5.task: Measure the impact of a given problem on system performance using a digital mini-calculator and visualize it with trend lines.
problem_solving.3.1.5.criterion: Measures the negative numerical impact of the problem, such as production/energy loss, etc. on the system using a digital mini- calculator and accurate mathematical metrics and presents the results in a clear trend graph.

problem_solving.3.1.6.objective: To develop alternative technical approaches to solve the problem and evaluate these alternatives in terms of feasibility.
problem_solving.3.1.6.task: Create at least three different solution concepts for an identified root cause as digital design cards, such as plans A, B, and C.
problem_solving.3.1.6.criterion: Enter at least three independent, innovative solution scenarios cards into the system that directly address the root cause, are technically feasible, and do not conflict with engineering principles.

problem_solving.3.1.7.objective: To compare solution alternatives according to criteria such as performance, cost, time, safety, quality, and sustainability.
problem_solving.3.1.7.task: Add alternative solution plans to the decision matrix module on the application and score them according to time, cost, and safety criteria.
problem_solving.3.1.7.criterion: Places the alternative solution plans into the decision matrix and evaluates each alternative with analytical and objective scores based on the system's cost, performance, and security constraints.

problem_solving.3.1.8.objective: To select the most appropriate solution based on a data-driven evaluation and support the selection with technical justifications.
problem_solving.3.1.8.task: Select the highest-scoring solution in the decision matrix and enter the digital justification document into the system, including quantitative analyses such as return on investment (ROI) and payback period.
problem_solving.3.1.8.criterion: Successfully defends the optimal solution derived from the matrix analysis with a strong digital business case based on numerical data and evidence, such as ROI and payback period. He uploads this document to the system.

problem_solving.3.1.9.objective: To present the results of the analysis and evaluation in an organized manner using graphs, tables, calculations, presentations, or technical reports.
problem_solving.3.1.9.task: Present a structured technical solution report dashboard, consisting of data tables, root cause diagrams, and a decision matrix, to the virtual project manager or mentor via the digital platform.
problem_solving.3.1.9.criterion: Presents all diagrams, tables, and numerical arguments in a visually coherent "Technical Solution Dashboard" format, suitable for professional engineering, for virtual approval.

problem_solving.3.1.10.objective: To evaluate the technical risks, uncertainties, and limitations that may arise during the implementation of the proposed solution.
problem_solving.3.1.10.task: Anticipate potential installation or safety challenges during the solution's field implementation by adding them to an interactive "Risk Assessment Table" on the digital platform.
problem_solving.3.1.10.criterion: Maps all technical and operational risk thresholds that may arise during the integration of the proposed solution in the field onto an interactive heat map with accurate severity values.

problem_solving.3.2.1.objective: To appropriately identify the technical problems determined within the scope of the project for solution development.
problem_solving.3.2.1.task: Virtually navigate through virtually generated project plans and PID diagrams to identify design conflicts and bottlenecks using markers.
problem_solving.3.2.1.criterion: By reviewing the virtual project plan (PID or CAD), accurately identifies and marks bottlenecks and design conflicts on the map that hinder the overall project flow.

problem_solving.3.2.2.objective: To evaluate the impact of the identified problem on project objectives, workflow, product quality, process efficiency, or system performance.
problem_solving.3.2.2.task: Calculate the quantitative impact of the identified bottlenecks on the project schedule and budget, such as days of delay, and enter the results into the virtual briefing module.
problem_solving.3.2.2.criterion: Accurately calculates the numerical impact of identified bottlenecks on the project's time and budget targets, causing delays or increasing costs, and transmits this data flawlessly to the briefing module.

problem_solving.3.2.3.objective: To develop multiple technical solution alternatives for the problem determined within the scope of the project.
problem_solving.3.2.3.task: Develop at least two innovative solution scenarios from different perspectives, such as design revision or process change, in the implementation scenario module.
problem_solving.3.2.3.criterion: To overcome project constraints, writes at least two independent, technically sound alternative scenarios that either manipulate the existing hardware or alter the process sequence. Then, uploads these into the relevant module in the system.

problem_solving.3.2.4.objective: To compare the proposed solution alternatives in terms of feasibility, cost, time, occupational safety, and technical competence.
problem_solving.3.2.4.task: Test the developed solutions using a cost-benefit analysis tool in the app to find the one that best suits the project constraints.
problem_solving.3.2.4.criterion: By inputting their solutions into a virtual cost-benefit analysis tool, analytically identifies the scenario that maximizes the project's work safety, time, and budget balance.

problem_solving.3.2.5.objective: To develop solution proposals that are compatible with current project conditions, organizational resources, existing equipment, and current procedures.
problem_solving.3.2.5.task: Solving a resource optimization puzzle that can be implemented within the existing workshop boundaries without requiring the purchase of external parts.
problem_solving.3.2.5.criterion: Without requiring any external procurement approval, builds a fully compatible and realistic solution by optimizing the limited resource pool of the virtual workshop provided by the application.

problem_solving.3.2.6.objective: To use observations, measurements, technical documents, standards, or field data when developing feasible solution proposals.
problem_solving.3.2.6.task: Linking international engineering standards (ISO, DIN, IEEE standards) from the digital library as references to the proposed solution.
problem_solving.3.2.6.criterion: Successfully links the proposed design to the most accurate manufacturer's catalog page or international engineering standard (ISO, DIN, IEEE standards) found in the digital archive.

problem_solving.3.2.7.objective: To explain the expected technical benefits and contribution of the selected solution proposal to the project process.
problem_solving.3.2.7.task: Predicting the benefits of the designed solution (e.g., a 15% increase in engine efficiency) using metrics and reflecting them in an interactive benefit table within the digital application.
problem_solving.3.2.7.criterion: Calculates the performance improvements or time savings that the solution will deliver in the field using sound engineering metrics (e.g., percentage increase) and presents them persuasively in a “benefits table” within the digital application.

problem_solving.3.2.8.objective: To identify the limitations, risks, and potential side effects that may arise during the implementation of the proposed solution.
problem_solving.3.2.8.task: Record any side effects the new solution might cause in existing modules (e.g., overheating, pressure fluctuations) as “warning notes” in the interactive system.
problem_solving.3.2.8.criterion: After the integration of the designed method, it anticipates potential technical side effects, such as pressure drop in other system modules and leaves appropriate warning notes within the system.

problem_solving.3.2.9.objective: To present the solution proposal, along with its technical justification, to the consultant, responsible engineer, or project team in a clear and understandable manner.
problem_solving.3.2.9.task: Present the elevator pitch (pitch & record) to the project team or virtual characters, including solution arguments and 3D CAD models, via the system.
problem_solving.3.2.9.criterion: Completes her 3D model- supported technical elevator presentation before the timer runs out, using sound engineering arguments and maintaining her excellent communication skills

problem_solving.3.2.10.objective: To review the solution proposal based on feedback received and adapt it to the scope of the project.
problem_solving.3.2.10.task: During the virtual review meeting, note the constructive technical feedback from other engineers in the digital agenda and revise the model.
problem_solving.3.2.10.criterion: Carefully filters revision requests and criticisms from the virtual evaluation jury, revising its model to perfectly match this specific technical feedback.

problem_solving.4.1.1.objective: To apply advanced analytical methods to identify the root causes of multidimensional and complex engineering problems.
problem_solving.4.1.1.task: Analysing and visualizing complex root-cause networks using data mining methods in a “Fault Tree Analysis (FTA)” simulation in the app.
problem_solving.4.1.1.criterion: Using the "Fault Tree Analysis (FTA)" algorithm in complex, multi- dimensional cases, maps interconnected main and sub-root cause networks without logical discontinuity.

problem_solving.4.1.2.objective: To design and formulate multiple alternative solutions for the identified complex problems.
problem_solving.4.1.2.task: Drawing innovative, feasible, and alternative concept designs for a multi-dimensional problem in an interactive modelling environment.
problem_solving.4.1.2.criterion: In large-scale crisis situations or complex design problems, builds two highly feasible, innovative, and completely different main scenario models (for example, Plan A and B) at the interface.

problem_solving.4.1.3.objective: To select the most appropriate solution by comparing the alternatives based on engineering constraints such as cost, time, performance, safety, etc.
problem_solving.4.1.3.task: Filtering the most optimal solution by weighting constraints such as time, cost, and security in the application's algorithmic decision matrix using a slider.
problem_solving.4.1.3.criterion: By adjusting the weighted decision matrix in the system to the optimal level based on the project’s strategic constraints, selects the mathematically best solution to the multi-variable equation.

problem_solving.4.1.4.objective: To anticipate technical, operational, and environmental risks that may arise during the implementation of developed solutions.
problem_solving.4.1.4.task: By fast-forwarding the simulation of the selected solution in the app, potential technical/environmental risks that may arise during installation are incorporated into a risk heatmap.
problem_solving.4.1.4.criterion: By running the solution simulation, instantly identifies hidden and long- term environmental and technical risks, and records them in the correct probability and impact zones on the comprehensive heatmap.

problem_solving.4.1.5.objective: To develop proactive preventive measures and emergency action plans to minimize identified risks.
problem_solving.4.1.5.task: Writing emergency action plans and proactive response strategies that can be activated through the system during a crisis for high- priority risks.
problem_solving.4.1.5.criterion: Logically loads “Emergency Protocols” into the system that safely shut down the system or switch it to an alternative path when risk scenarios in the red zone occur.

problem_solving.4.1.6.objective: To test the validity of solutions using simulation, computer- aided modeling, or prototyping tools.
problem_solving.4.1.6.task: The selected solution is built in a virtual simulation environment and validated by subjecting it to various stress, leakage, and load test scenarios.
problem_solving.4.1.6.criterion: Places the digital prototype in a virtual stress environment and proves the validity of its solution by accurately analysing the design’s failure points in the out-of-limit leakage/load simulations it performs.

problem_solving.4.1.7.objective: To establish a holistic and integrated solution architecture by breaking down problems requiring multidisciplinary approaches into subsystems.
problem_solving.4.1.7.task: Dividing multidisciplinary problems into subsystems, such as mechanical, software, etc. and establishing a holistic architecture by mapping inter-module connection diagrams on the interface.
problem_solving.4.1.7.criterion: Combines subsystem modules from different engineering disciplines such as software, automation, mechanics in a way that fully complies with logical interface rules, creating a complete and functional integrated architecture.

problem_solving.4.1.8.objective: To analyse the impacts of integrating developed solutions into existing systems and resolve any incompatibilities.
problem_solving.4.1.8.task: Running a simulation to integrate the newly developed module into the existing system infrastructure and correcting any potential conflicts.
problem_solving.4.1.8.criterion: During the integration of the new solution, instantly detects and resolves any data or physical connection conflicts with the old system, leaving zero errors.

problem_solving.4.1.9.objective: To identify bottlenecks and propose sustainable improvement plans to enhance the system’s long-term performance.
problem_solving.4.1.9.task: Identify capacity limits by analysing long-term system logs and data within the application and design a plan for a permanent system upgrade rather than a temporary fix. Upload the plan to the application.
problem_solving.4.1.9.criterion: By filtering the system’s large volume of log data using the right analysis tools, identifies long-term chronic bottlenecks and, rather than applying patches to the system, designs a long-term capacity-enhancement plan and uploads this plan to the system.

problem_solving.4.1.10.objective: To follow current literature and emerging technologies and adapt innovative and non- standard solution methods to the problem.
problem_solving.4.1.10.task: Explain how an innovative technology can be adapted to a specific problem by searching current papers and patent databases and upload this information to the system.
problem_solving.4.1.10.criterion: In situations where standard procedures are insufficient, successfully adapts a cutting- edge innovation (for example, AI) found in the digital patent or paper library into the simulation environment.

problem_solving.4.2.1.objective: To provide guidance and direction to team members on systematic problem-solving techniques.
problem_solving.4.2.1.task: Create an interactive guide document (virtual tutorial) explaining problem-solving tools for lower-level (L1 or L2) trainee profiles. Upload this to the application.
problem_solving.4.2.1.criterion: transforms complex problem- solving tools into an interactive digital guide with the simplicity and accuracy that virtual users at the L1 or L2 levels can understand.

problem_solving.4.2.2.objective: To lead the team in collaboratively developing a solution by facilitating group brainstorming sessions.
problem_solving.4.2.2.task: As a moderator, lead a virtual brainstorming session designed within the app, categorize the idea bubbles on the screen, and guide the team toward consensus.
problem_solving.4.2.2.criterion: During the virtual session she moderates, successfully groups the ideas that appear on the screen within a logical framework and, by encouraging passive virtual participants, guides the team toward the targeted, collaborative innovative solution.

problem_solving.4.2.3.objective: To provide constructive feedback to less experienced interns or junior team members on problem diagnosis and resolution.
problem_solving.4.2.3.task: Reading diagnostic analysis reports from lower levels (L1 or L2) into the system via a digital rubric and writing constructive and helpful feedback.
problem_solving.4.2.3.criterion: Identifies technical errors in incoming diagnostic reports with an objective and keen eye using a checklist. Provides feedback that is non- confrontational, professional, constructive, and based entirely on technical arguments.

problem_solving.4.2.4.objective: To document the stages of resolved problems and the lessons learned for the organization’s knowledge base.
problem_solving.4.2.4.task: Submit a digital report in "Lessons Learned" format for successfully closed cases to the organization's knowledge base for approval.
problem_solving.4.2.4.criterion: Converts the technical experience gained from the crisis and the successful steps taken to resolve it into a structured “Lessons Learned” document that other engineers can easily find and apply using a search engine. Uploads this to the system.

problem_solving.4.2.5.objective: To analyse existing inefficiencies in the problem-solving process and propose recommendations to accelerate the process or improve quality.
problem_solving.4.2.5.task: Identify inefficiencies in the team’s problem-solving steps using the system’s process map and highlight areas for optimization.
problem_solving.4.2.5.criterion: Provides a bird's-eye view of the current operational process map used by the team. By pinpointing instances of resource waste, repetitive approvals, or unnecessary waiting steps, maps out concrete optimization paths.

problem_solving.4.2.6.objective: To systematically monitor the results of solution implementation and conduct process improvement initiatives using the data obtained.
problem_solving.4.2.6.task: After implementing the solution, track real-time metrics from the field using the application dashboard and assign continuous improvement goals.
problem_solving.4.2.6.criterion: After the solution is deployed, it algorithmically analyses the real-time performance data displayed on the live- dashboard screen and sets new continuous improvement targets for the system to address any deviations.

problem_solving.4.2.7.objective: To promote a culture of collaborative problem- solving by fostering effective communication among team members from diverse disciplines.
problem_solving.4.2.7.task: To break down complex technical information into a level that people with varying levels of expertise can understand by creating visuals and graphics, and upload these in the app.
problem_solving.4.2.7.criterion: Create visuals and graphics to present detailed engineering calculations in a format that people with varying levels of expertise can understand and implement them. In this way, to build a bridge of communication during virtual meetings.

problem_solving.4.2.8.objective: To contribute to the conversion of successful solution strategies into standard operating procedures.
problem_solving.4.2.8.task: Using the “Procedure Designer Module” within the application, transform a successful solution strategy into a permanent and sustainable standard procedure that everyone will follow.
problem_solving.4.2.8.criterion: Transforms an innovative intervention that has achieved one-time success into a standardized, step-by-step operational guide that can be implemented on every shift, using the system’s procedure designer tool.

problem_solving.4.2.9.objective: To design and advocate for systemic changes embedded within the process to prevent the recurrence of encountered errors.
problem_solving.4.2.9.task: Design an in-system error- prevention mechanism that will fundamentally prevent identified hardware or human errors and upload this mechanism to the application.
problem_solving.4.2.9.criterion: Logically constructs a hardware or software “Poka- Yoke (Error-Proofing)” circuit, designed with technical ingenuity, that will reduce the likelihood of chronic human or systematic errors observed in the system to zero.

problem_solving.4.2.10.objective: To manage stakeholder expectations during the resolution of complex problems and professionally report outcomes to senior management.
problem_solving.4.2.10.task: Preparing and uploading a comprehensive professional “Management Report” that includes a cost-benefit analysis and technical progress and presenting it to virtual stakeholders.
problem_solving.4.2.10.criterion: Prepares a highly calibrated, data-driven, and persuasive professional Executive Report that balances the investment and profit expectations (ROI) of senior management with technical realities during the crisis resolution process, and uploads it to the system.

communication.2.1.9.task: Explain a basic engineering requirement to a member of the administrative or HR team.
communication.2.1.9.criterion: Explanation is jargon-free and easily understood by the recipient.

communication.2.1.10.task: Maintain appropriate eye contact and posture during a one-on-one performance review.
communication.2.1.10.criterion: Non-verbal cues demonstrate attentiveness and professionalism.

communication.2.2.1.task: Write an email to the IT department requesting software access, using standard formatting.
communication.2.2.1.criterion: Email includes a clear subject line, polite request, and formal sign-off.

communication.2.2.2.task: Draft bullet-point minutes for a 30- minute team meeting and distribute to attendees.
communication.2.2.2.criterion: Minutes accurately capture decisions made and outline next steps.

communication.2.2.3.task: Document the steps taken to resolve a minor technical issue in the project tracker.
communication.2.2.3.criterion: Description is sequential, logical, and easy for another engineer to follow.

communication.2.2.4.task: Draft a weekly end-of-week summary email detailing personal accomplishments and next week's goals.
communication.2.2.4.criterion: Report is structured correctly and free of grammatical errors.

communication.2.2.5.task: Post a project update in the main team channel summarizing a reached milestone.
communication.2.2.5.criterion: Message is enthusiastic yet professional, utilizing appropriate tagging (@).

communication.2.2.6.task: Draft an email to a senior engineer outlining a problem and proposing a potential solution for review.
communication.2.2.6.criterion: Email clearly separates the problem statement from the proposed solution.

communication.2.2.7.task: Review and correct a draft technical memo for spelling, grammar, and tone before sending.
communication.2.2.7.criterion: Final memo is error-free and maintains a professional tone.

communication.2.2.8.task: Draft a one-page 'How-To' guide for operating a specific piece of lab equipment.
communication.2.2.8.criterion: Guide is easy to read, uses bullet points, and includes safety warnings.

communication.2.2.9.task: Reply to an email from a colleague asking for data, providing the information clearly and concisely.
communication.2.2.9.criterion: Response directly answers the question without unnecessary elaboration.

communication.2.2.10.task: Populate a standard risk assessment form with relevant data for a new project phase.
communication.2.2.10.criterion: Form is filled out completely, adhering strictly to the template's constraints.

communication.3.1.1.task: Create a slide deck to support a 10- minute presentation on research findings.
communication.3.1.1.criterion: Slides are visually clean, not text-heavy, and highlight key data points.

communication.3.1.2.task: Present the results of a material testing cycle to the immediate project team.
communication.3.1.2.criterion: Presentation is delivered smoothly, adhering to the allotted time limit.

communication.3.1.3.task: Explain the rationale behind a design change to both a senior engineer and an administrative manager.
communication.3.1.3.criterion: Explanation is appropriately technical for the engineer and simplified for the manager.

communication.3.1.4.task: Respond to peer questions effectively following a brief technical presentation.
communication.3.1.4.criterion: Answers are clear, direct, and admit when further research is needed.

communication.3.1.5.task: Present a monthly expense report using charts to highlight trends rather than just raw numbers.
communication.3.1.5.criterion: Data presentation clearly illustrates the core narrative or trend.

communication.3.1.6.task: Pitch a minor process improvement idea to the supervisor using a structured proposal format.
communication.3.1.6.criterion: Pitch clearly defines the problem, solution, cost, and benefit.

communication.3.1.7.task: Verbally outline the potential risks associated with a new software implementation during a meeting.
communication.3.1.7.criterion: Risks are communicated objectively without causing unnecessary alarm.

communication.3.1.8.task: Conduct a live demonstration of a newly developed CAD model to the design team.
communication.3.1.8.criterion: Demonstration is easy to follow and highlights the model's key features.

communication.3.1.9.task: Defend a specific material choice during a design review using data and logical reasoning.
communication.3.1.9.criterion: Defense relies on facts and remains respectful of opposing viewpoints.

communication.3.1.10.task: Present a 5-minute summary of a recently published industry paper relevant to the team's work.
communication.3.1.10.criterion: Summary captures the paper's core thesis and its practical application to the project.

communication.3.2.1.task: Create and distribute an agenda for a small sub-team check-in meeting 24 hours in advance.
communication.3.2.1.criterion: Agenda includes topics, time allocations, and required preparations.

communication.3.2.2.task: Lead a 15-minute stand-up, ensuring all members speak and the meeting ends on time.
communication.3.2.2.criterion: Meeting stays on topic and concludes within the scheduled window.

communication.3.2.3.task: Guide a team brainstorming session to solve a minor logistical issue.
communication.3.2.3.criterion: Facilitator encourages participation from all members and notes all ideas.

communication.3.2.4.task: Politely redirect the conversation when a meeting topic begins to drift off-agenda.
communication.3.2.4.criterion: Redirection is handled professionally, keeping the meeting focused.

communication.3.2.5.task: Summarize the key decisions made at the end of a discussion before adjourning.
communication.3.2.5.criterion: Summary accurately reflects the consensus reached by the group.

communication.3.2.6.task: Verbally confirm who is responsible for which task at the close of a planning meeting.
communication.3.2.6.criterion: Action items are assigned clearly with agreed-upon deadlines.
