communication.3.2.7.task: Mediate a brief debate between two peers regarding a design choice to reach a compromise.
communication.3.2.7.criterion: Mediation remains neutral and focuses on project goals over personal opinions.

communication.3.2.8.task: Host a video conference call, managing screen sharing and participant muting effectively.
communication.3.2.8.criterion: Call runs smoothly without technical interruptions caused by the host.

communication.3.2.9.task: Directly, yet politely, ask for input from a team member who hasn't spoken during a review.
communication.3.2.9.criterion: Action successfully brings diverse viewpoints into the discussion.

communication.3.2.10.task: Send a follow-up email two days after a meeting to check on the status of delegated tasks.
communication.3.2.10.criterion: Email serves as a polite reminder and offers assistance if needed.

communication.4.1.1.task: Draft an email updating a supplier on a delayed shipment, for supervisor review.
communication.4.1.1.criterion: Draft requires minimal edits and adopts an appropriate external tone.

communication.4.1.2.task: Introduce oneself and provide a brief status update during a scheduled client video call.
communication.4.1.2.criterion: Update is professional, reassuring, and avoids overpromising.

communication.4.1.3.task: Compile a monthly progress report formatted specifically for a client's review.
communication.4.1.3.criterion: Report meets all external branding and formatting guidelines.

communication.4.1.4.task: Respond to a basic technical question from a vendor regarding a part specification.
communication.4.1.4.criterion: Response is accurate and represents the company professionally.

communication.4.1.5.task: Explain a complex engineering constraint to a non-technical client during a meeting.
communication.4.1.5.criterion: Client confirms understanding without feeling overwhelmed by jargon.

communication.4.1.6.task: Draft a communication politely explaining why a requested feature falls outside the project scope.
communication.4.1.6.criterion: Communication is firm, polite, and references the original contract/scope.

communication.4.1.7.task: Interact professionally with contractors while collecting data during an external site visit.
communication.4.1.7.criterion: Interactions are respectful and adhere to site protocols.

communication.4.1.8.task: Draft a section of a project proposal intended for a potential new client.
communication.4.1.8.criterion: Section is persuasive, technically sound, and aligns with the proposal's overall voice.

communication.4.1.9.task: Create a polished slide deck for a project handover meeting with the client.
communication.4.1.9.criterion: Deck is high-quality, comprehensive, and tailored to stakeholder interests.

communication.4.1.10.task: Draft a 'Thank You' and next-steps email following an initial meeting with a new vendor.
communication.4.1.10.criterion: Email builds rapport and clearly outlines the agreed- upon next steps.

communication.4.2.1.task: Listen to critical feedback on a failed task during a 1-on-1 and outline a plan for improvement.
communication.4.2.1.criterion: Feedback is received without defensiveness and applied to future work.

communication.4.2.2.task: Inform the project team of a significant technical failure that will delay the schedule.
communication.4.2.2.criterion: News is delivered promptly, objectively, and accompanied by a mitigation plan.

communication.4.2.3.task: Request additional lab time from a lab manager whose schedule is already fully booked.
communication.4.2.3.criterion: Request is made politely, offering flexibility and demonstrating valid need.

communication.4.2.4.task: Draft a calming, objective response to an overly aggressive email from a frustrated colleague.
communication.4.2.4.criterion: Response sticks to facts, avoids emotional escalation, and proposes a meeting to resolve.

communication.4.2.5.task: Argue for the adoption of a specific software tool despite pushback from team members.
communication.4.2.5.criterion: Argument is persistent but respectful, relying on cost- benefit data.

communication.4.2.6.task: Politely decline a peer's request to add an extra feature to a nearly completed model.
communication.4.2.6.criterion: Declination cites timeline constraints and prioritizes project completion.

communication.4.2.7.task: Report an observed safety protocol breach to the supervisor formally and objectively.
communication.4.2.7.criterion: Report is factual, timely, and free of personal accusations.

communication.4.2.8.task: Apologize for and correct a miscommunicated instruction that led to a minor error.
communication.4.2.8.criterion: Apology takes ownership of the mistake and clarifies the correct procedure.

communication.4.2.9.task: Constructively communicate to a supervisor that a given deadline is unachievable.
communication.4.2.9.criterion: Communication provides evidence of the workload and suggests a realistic alternative.

communication.4.2.10.task: Write a formal email summarizing the agreed resolution following a conflict regarding task ownership.
communication.4.2.10.criterion: Summary is agreed upon by all parties and prevents future misunderstandings.

ethics.1.1.1.objective: Learn what safety rules and attendance expectations exist in the host company.
ethics.1.1.1.task: Read through the company safety handbook from first da. Write down the main rules and required arrival times. Log the checklist in EngineerTrack and share it with your mentor by end of day.
ethics.1.1.1.criterion: Mentor reviews the checklist in EngineerTrack. At least 8 rules are correctly noted and the attendance times are accurate.

ethics.1.1.2.objective: Understand why arrival on time matters in a real engineering workplace.
ethics.1.1.2.task: Record your arrival and departure times daily in EngineerTrack for the first two weeks. Submit the log to your supervisor each Friday through the app.
ethics.1.1.2.criterion: Supervisor checks the log in EngineerTrack. No days are missing and times match the actual attendance record.

ethics.1.1.3.objective: Know what may happen when safety rules are broken at workplace.
ethics.1.1.3.task: Attend the safety induction. Afterwards write a one-page reflection in EngineerTrack identifying three consequences of non-compliance based on what was discussed.
ethics.1.1.3.criterion: The reflection names three realistic consequences that match what was covered in the induction, confirmed by the supervisor in the app.

ethics.1.1.4.objective: Tell the difference between safety equipment that is required and guidance that is only recommended.
ethics.1.1.4.task: Watch a senior engineer do the daily safety check. Record each piece of PPE in EngineerTrack, marking each as required or optional.
ethics.1.1.4.criterion: Supervisor checks the list in EngineerTrack. Every item is correctly marked and nothing important is missing.

ethics.1.1.5.objective: Know the steps to follow when you spot a hazard at work.
ethics.1.1.5.task: Spend a morning with the health and safety officer. Log every step of the hazard-reporting procedure in EngineerTrack in the order they were demonstrated.
ethics.1.1.5.criterion: The logged steps match the official reporting procedure. All steps are present and in the right order, verified by the supervisor.

ethics.1.1.6.objective: Notice what professional behaviour looks like day to day in an engineering office.
ethics.1.1.6.task: During your first week, log three examples of professional responsibility shown by colleagues in EngineerTrack. Add a short note for each explaining why it matters.
ethics.1.1.6.criterion: Supervisor reads the three entries. Each one is a real, concrete example and the explanation makes sense.

ethics.1.1.7.objective: Get a basic idea of what sustainability means in everyday work life.
ethics.1.1.7.task: Sit in on one team meeting where sustainability comes up. Log at least two specific practices mentioned by the team in EngineerTrack.
ethics.1.1.7.criterion: The logged notes name two practices clearly. A short comment is added on what each one achieves in terms of reducing impact.

ethics.1.1.8.objective: Remember the emergency exit procedure for your work area.
ethics.1.1.8.task: Take part in a fire drill. Right after it ends, log every step from the alarm to the all-clear in EngineerTrack from memory.
ethics.1.1.8.criterion: All key steps are logged in the right order in EngineerTrack. No reference materials were used, confirmed by supervisor.

ethics.1.1.9.objective: Find out who in the organisation is responsible for safety and ethics.
ethics.1.1.9.task: Using the company organisation chart, identify at least three people responsible for safety or ethics. Log their names and roles in EngineerTrack.
ethics.1.1.9.criterion: Three people correctly identified with accurate job titles, verified by supervisor through the app.

ethics.1.1.10.objective: See the connection between showing up on time and how the team works.
ethics.1.1.10.task: Talk to one supervisor or experienced colleague about punctuality. Log a 150-word summary of the conversation in EngineerTrack and submit it to your mentor.
ethics.1.1.10.criterion: The summary reflects what the colleague said, includes one concrete example, and was submitted on time as recorded in EngineerTrack.

ethics.1.2.1.objective: Spot the ethical rules and standards that apply to the current project.
ethics.1.2.1.task: Go through the project brief and related documents. Log every ethical guideline, code of conduct reference, or compliance requirement you find in EngineerTrack.
ethics.1.2.1.criterion: At least three ethical references correctly identified. For each one, a one-sentence note explains why it matters, visible in EngineerTrack for supervisor review.

ethics.1.2.2.objective: Notice when and how sustainability goals show up in an active project.
ethics.1.2.2.task: Attend a project meeting. Take notes focused on sustainability targets or commitments. Log at least two in EngineerTrack with a brief explanation of how the team is working towards each.
ethics.1.2.2.criterion: Notes contain at least two sustainability goals logged in EngineerTrack. Supervising engineer confirms accuracy through the app.

ethics.1.2.3.objective: Understand the difference between what engineers must do ethically and what is just good practice.
ethics.1.2.3.task: Read part of a relevant engineering code of ethics. Create a two-column table in EngineerTrack: one column for obligatory rules, one for recommended practices. Add at least five entries.
ethics.1.2.3.criterion: Table has five or more entries correctly placed. Each entry has a short reason why it belongs there, reviewable by mentor in EngineerTrack.

ethics.1.2.4.objective: Learn which sustainability practices are used in day-to-day project work.
ethics.1.2.4.task: Observe how materials and waste are handled on the current project. Log descriptions of three specific practices in EngineerTrack.
ethics.1.2.4.criterion: Three practices described clearly in EngineerTrack. Each one linked to a sustainability principle. Submitted by agreed deadline as tracked in the app.

ethics.1.2.5.objective: Recognise when a personal interest might get in the way of doing the right thing professionally.
ethics.1.2.5.task: Read a case study about an engineering ethics dilemma. Log a short paragraph in EngineerTrack identifying the conflict and the parties affected.
ethics.1.2.5.criterion: Paragraph correctly names the conflict and at least two affected parties. The explanation shows understanding of why it is a problem, reviewed by supervisor.

ethics.1.2.6.objective: Know what confidentiality and data privacy mean for someone in an internship.
ethics.1.2.6.task: Read the organisation's data privacy policy or NDA. Write a plain one- page summary of key obligations and upload it to EngineerTrack.
ethics.1.2.6.criterion: Summary covers the main obligations correctly. Written in simple language. Mentor reviews and approves it in EngineerTrack.

ethics.1.2.7.objective: See how environmental concerns shape decisions in an engineering project.
ethics.1.2.7.task: Sit in on or read notes from an environmental review meeting. Log three decisions that were shaped by environmental factors in EngineerTrack.
ethics.1.2.7.criterion: Three decisions are logged. Each includes a note on which environmental concern drove it, confirmed by supervising engineer.

ethics.1.2.8.objective: Understand why getting data right matters from an ethical point of view.
ethics.1.2.8.task: Join a data quality review session. Log the verification steps used by the team in EngineerTrack and add a note on what happens if mistakes are made.
ethics.1.2.8.criterion: Steps logged in the right order. One consequence of data errors is noted, showing the intern understood why accuracy matters, reviewed by supervisor.

ethics.1.2.9.objective: Find out if there are more sustainable options for the materials being used in the project.
ethics.1.2.9.task: Make a list of materials or resources used in your current task in EngineerTrack. Next to each, note whether a more sustainable option exists based on observation or brief research.
ethics.1.2.9.criterion: At least five items listed. A sustainability note must be given for each. At least one outside source cited, visible in EngineerTrack.

ethics.1.2.10.objective: Get a basic understanding of corporate social responsibility and how it relates to the host company.
ethics.1.2.10.task: Find the company's CSR or sustainability report. Prepare five key points and log them in EngineerTrack, highlighting two relevant to engineering work. Present them to your mentor.
ethics.1.2.10.criterion: Five points logged and presented. Two engineering- relevant points clearly highlighted. Intern answers at least two follow-up questions correctly, outcome logged by mentor.

ethics.2.1.1.objective: Plan your work for the week and get tasks done within the times agreed with your supervisor.
ethics.2.1.1.task: At the start of every week, create a task plan in EngineerTrack listing all assigned tasks, estimated durations, and agreed deadlines. Update status each day.
ethics.2.1.1.criterion: Plan updated every week in EngineerTrack. At least 80% of tasks completed by their deadlines, confirmed by supervisor through the app.

ethics.2.1.2.objective: Follow safety checks every time you start a new task, not just the ones that seem risky.
ethics.2.1.2.task: Before starting any task, complete the pre-task safety checklist in EngineerTrack and submit it to your supervisor before beginning work.
ethics.2.1.2.criterion: A checklist submitted in EngineerTrack before every task. No items left blank or incorrect. Supervisor verifies through the app.

ethics.2.1.3.objective: Decide which task to do first when you have several tasks to do in the same time.
ethics.2.1.3.task: When given three or more tasks at the same time, create a priority matrix in EngineerTrack using urgent versus important as your axes. Share it with your supervisor before starting.
ethics.2.1.3.criterion: Priority matrix produced in EngineerTrack for each multi-task situation. Supervisor agrees with the proposed order in at least 80% of cases. Tasks completed in that order.

ethics.2.1.4.objective: Keep your supervisor informed about how work is going and flag problems early on.
ethics.2.1.4.task: Send a short daily status update through EngineerTrack every working day, three to five points covering what you did and any risk of delay.
ethics.2.1.4.criterion: Updates sent on at least 90% of working days in EngineerTrack. Accurate content. Any delay risk is flagged at least one day before the deadline, confirmed by supervisor.

ethics.2.1.5.objective: Follow a Standard Operating Procedure properly when carrying out a routine task.
ethics.2.1.5.task: Pick one routine task with an SOP. Follow it step by step and log each completed step in EngineerTrack as you go.
ethics.2.1.5.criterion: Task log in EngineerTrack shows every step completed in the right order. Nothing skipped. Supervisor checks against the official SOP.

ethics.2.1.6.objective: Get better at estimating how long tasks will actually take.
ethics.2.1.6.task: Before each new task, log your time estimate and reasoning in EngineerTrack. When finished, log the actual time taken and note the difference.
ethics.2.1.6.criterion: Done for at least four tasks in EngineerTrack. Estimates within 20% of actual time on at least three occasions. Notes show progressive learning from the gaps.

ethics.2.1.7.objective: Spot problems with quality during routine work and report them straight away.
ethics.2.1.7.task: Use the quality checklist in EngineerTrack while doing each task. If something falls short of the standard, log it and notify your supervisor through the app the same day.
ethics.2.1.7.criterion: All significant quality problems reported within two hours via EngineerTrack. Written record accurate. Supervisor confirms through the app.

ethics.2.1.8.objective: Handle sensitive project information carefully and keep it confidential.
ethics.2.1.8.task: For any task involving confidential data, add a note in EngineerTrack confirming which data-handling protocol was followed.
ethics.2.1.8.criterion: Every relevant task entry in EngineerTrack includes this note. Supervisor confirms no breaches occurred during the supervised period.

ethics.2.1.9.objective: Write up what happened after each task is finished.
ethics.2.1.9.task: When a task is done, complete the outcome record in EngineerTrack: task description, time taken, result achieved, and any problems encountered.
ethics.2.1.9.criterion: Outcome record submitted in EngineerTrack for every task. All fields filled. Submitted within one hour of finishing. Supervisor verifies.

ethics.2.1.10.objective: Look back at your week and work out what you could do differently next time.
ethics.2.1.10.task: Every Friday, complete the weekly self-evaluation form in EngineerTrack: tasks planned versus done, reasons for anything not finished, and one improvement for next week. Discuss with supervisor.
ethics.2.1.10.criterion: Form submitted every Friday in EngineerTrack without being reminded. Supervisor confirms the reflection is honest and the improvement point is genuine.

ethics.2.2.1.objective: Apply the right industry standard when working on any task you are given.
ethics.2.2.1.task: Before starting a task, find the applicable standard, note its number and key requirements in EngineerTrack, and complete the task in compliance with it.
ethics.2.2.1.criterion: Correct standard identified and logged for at least 80% of tasks in EngineerTrack. Supervisor confirms work met the standard's requirements in each case.

ethics.2.2.2.objective: Write emails, notes, and reports in a way that is professional and appropriate for an engineering workplace.
ethics.2.2.2.task: Draft all task-related communications professionally. Upload the first three to EngineerTrack for mentor review before sending.
ethics.2.2.2.criterion: Mentor finds no significant issues with the first three in EngineerTrack. Later communications on time with no concerns from the supervisor.

ethics.2.2.3.objective: See how professional codes of conduct shape real decisions during the working week.
ethics.2.2.3.task: Read the relevant professional code of conduct. Each day, log one short note in EngineerTrack on how something in the code affected a decision you made.
ethics.2.2.3.criterion: At least four notes logged over the week in EngineerTrack. Each links a specific code provision to a specific decision. Supervisor validates.

ethics.2.2.4.objective: Make sure data is recorded correctly by having someone else check it.
ethics.2.2.4.task: For every piece of data you record, ask a colleague or supervisor to check it. Log who checked it and the result in EngineerTrack.
ethics.2.2.4.criterion: Every data entry has a second check recorded in EngineerTrack. No entries left unchecked. Supervisor confirms at end of each week.

ethics.2.2.5.objective: Choose materials or methods that are better for the environment when you have a choice.
ethics.2.2.5.task: When you have two or more options for a material or method, use the decision matrix in EngineerTrack to score each against environmental criteria. Log the choice and the reason.
ethics.2.2.5.criterion: Decision matrix completed in EngineerTrack for at least two choices. Supervisor agrees the selection is environmentally sound.

ethics.2.2.6.objective: Do a safety check before every new type of task, even routine ones.
ethics.2.2.6.task: Fill in a brief written risk assessment in EngineerTrack before each new type of task. Submit to supervisor through the app before starting.
ethics.2.2.6.criterion: Risk assessment submitted in EngineerTrack before every new task type. None missing or incomplete. Supervisor confirms.

ethics.2.2.7.objective: Know when something is beyond what you are allowed to decide on your own and ask for help.
ethics.2.2.7.task: If a task requires a decision beyond your current scope, log the situation in EngineerTrack and notify your supervisor through the app immediately before proceeding.
ethics.2.2.7.criterion: At least two such situations correctly identified and escalated in EngineerTrack. Supervisor confirms no unauthorised decisions were made.

ethics.2.2.8.objective: Deliver your work to colleagues on time and let them know when it is ready.
ethics.2.2.8.task: Track every output owed to a team member in EngineerTrack. When you deliver it, log a delivery confirmation in the app straight away.
ethics.2.2.8.criterion: 90% of outputs delivered on time. Delivery confirmation logged in EngineerTrack in 100% of cases. Verified by supervisor and team member records.

ethics.2.2.9.objective: Stay within the boundaries of what you are supposed to be doing each week.
ethics.2.2.9.task: At the start of each week, confirm your scope of work with your supervisor in EngineerTrack. Flag any request that appears to fall outside it through the app.
ethics.2.2.9.criterion: Scope confirmed in EngineerTrack for at least 90% of weeks. Any out-of- scope requests flagged. Supervisor confirms.

ethics.2.2.10.objective: Check your own work against quality standards before handing it in.
ethics.2.2.10.task: Before submitting any output, complete the self-audit checklist in EngineerTrack and attach it to the submission in the app.
ethics.2.2.10.criterion: Checklist attached to every submission in EngineerTrack. Supervisor's own check finds the intern correctly spotted any gaps in at least 80% of submissions.

ethics.3.1.1.objective: Build a personal system for managing your time across several tasks at once, without needing your supervisor to chase you.
ethics.3.1.1.task: At the start of each two-week period, create your own work plan in EngineerTrack listing all tasks, durations, dependencies, and deadlines. Share it with your supervisor before they ask.
ethics.3.1.1.criterion: Plan shared in EngineerTrack at the start of every cycle without a reminder. Supervisor says it is realistic. At least 90% of tasks finished on time.

ethics.3.1.2.objective: Figure out on your own what caused a deadline to be at risk and fix it.
ethics.3.1.2.task: When a deadline is in danger at least 48 hours before it is due, log a root-cause analysis and recovery plan in EngineerTrack. Put the plan into action and report the outcome through the app.
ethics.3.1.2.criterion: Deadline risks spotted at least 48 hours early in at least 80% of situations without supervisor prompting. Recovery plan logged in EngineerTrack and confirmed as appropriate.

ethics.3.1.3.objective: Take full responsibility for the commitments you make to colleagues and others.
ethics.3.1.3.task: Keep a running commitment log in EngineerTrack of every timing promise made to any team member or stakeholder. Review it daily and follow up on anything coming due soon.
ethics.3.1.3.criterion: Log updated every day in EngineerTrack. No commitment missed without advance notice. Supervisor confirms.

ethics.3.1.4.objective: Think ahead about which tasks might take longer than planned and adjust before it becomes a problem.
ethics.3.1.4.task: At the start of each week, rate every task as High, Medium, or Low risk in EngineerTrack based on complexity. Allocate extra time in the plan to high-risk ones.
ethics.3.1.4.criterion: Risk-rated plan produced independently in EngineerTrack each week. Supervisor agrees ratings make sense in at least 85% of plans. Actual outcomes confirm the ratings.

ethics.3.1.5.objective: Show up on time every day and maintain that habit throughout the advanced phase.
ethics.3.1.5.task: Keep a clean attendance record logged in EngineerTrack for the whole advanced phase. If something unexpected happens, notify your supervisor and affected colleagues through the app as early as possible.
ethics.3.1.5.criterion: No unexplained late arrivals or absences in EngineerTrack during the advanced phase. Any exceptions communicated early. Supervisor confirms.

ethics.3.1.6.objective: Reflect honestly on how well your time management is working and make real changes.
ethics.3.1.6.task: At the end of each two-week cycle, log a short review in EngineerTrack: what worked, what did not, and one specific thing you will do differently. Share key points with your supervisor.
ethics.3.1.6.criterion: Review logged in EngineerTrack at end of every cycle. Supervisor confirms a real improvement is applied in the next cycle across at least three consecutive cycles.

ethics.3.1.7.objective: Build sustainability checks into your planning when tasks involve physical resources.
ethics.3.1.7.task: When planning any task that uses materials, equipment, or energy, add a sustainability check step in EngineerTrack with time allocated for verifying responsible resource use.
ethics.3.1.7.criterion: Sustainability check step included in the plan for every relevant task in EngineerTrack. Supervisor confirms checks are genuine and at least one real improvement results.

ethics.3.1.8.objective: Handle unexpected extra tasks without letting your existing commitments slip.
ethics.3.1.8.task: When an unplanned task is assigned, assess its impact on your current plan independently and log the re-prioritisation decision in EngineerTrack. Negotiate revised timelines if needed through the app.
ethics.3.1.8.criterion: Unplanned tasks handled independently in at least 80% of cases. Existing commitments met or renegotiated in advance in 100% of cases. Supervisor confirms in EngineerTrack.

ethics.3.1.9.objective: Report your progress honestly each week without overstating what has been done.
ethics.3.1.9.task: Every Friday, submit a weekly progress report in EngineerTrack, clearly separating tasks done, in progress, and not started. Give real reasons for anything incomplete.
ethics.3.1.9.criterion: Reports submitted every Friday in EngineerTrack without prompting. Spot- check finds no difference between reported and actual status in at least 90% of reports.

ethics.3.1.10.objective: Have a clear plan ready for when several urgent deadlines land at the same time.
ethics.3.1.10.task: Whenever two or more high- priority deadlines fall within 24 hours of each other, log a contingency plan in EngineerTrack before that point. Include escalation path and resource needs. Share with supervisor.
ethics.3.1.10.criterion: Contingency plan logged in EngineerTrack for every such situation without being asked. Supervisor rates it adequate or better in at least 80% of cases. Outcomes confirm it worked.

ethics.3.2.1.objective: Use a proper ethical reasoning approach when a technical decision involves a moral dimension.
ethics.3.2.1.task: When a technical choice has an ethical side, log your reasoning in EngineerTrack: framework used, options considered, stakeholders affected, decision made, and why. Share with supervisor.
ethics.3.2.1.criterion: At least three such records logged in EngineerTrack during the advanced phase. Supervisor confirms reasoning is sound, stakeholders correctly identified, and decision is ethically justifiable.

ethics.3.2.2.objective: Compare technical options on environmental grounds and choose the one with the smallest footprint.
ethics.3.2.2.task: When you have two or more ways to solve a technical problem, log a comparison in EngineerTrack covering energy use, material waste, and lifecycle impact. Record choice and rationale.
ethics.3.2.2.criterion: Comparison logged in EngineerTrack for at least two choices. Supervisor confirms method is sound and option chosen is most sustainable among those feasible.

ethics.3.2.3.objective: Take personal responsibility for the quality of your technical work without waiting for someone else to check it.
ethics.3.2.3.task: Before submitting any technical output, audit it against the relevant standard. Log a signed self- declaration in EngineerTrack confirming it meets requirements and attach it to the submission.
ethics.3.2.3.criterion: Signed declaration attached to every technical submission in EngineerTrack. Supervisor's spot-check finds no quality failures in at least 85% of reviewed submissions.

ethics.3.2.4.objective: Think about how a technical solution might affect different groups of people.
ethics.3.2.4.task: For one assigned technical task, research how the solution could affect different users. Log two social sustainability considerations in EngineerTrack and explain how each influenced your approach.
ethics.3.2.4.criterion: Two social sustainability points logged in EngineerTrack for the task. Supervisor confirms they are genuine, relevant, and actually influenced the technical decision.

ethics.3.2.5.objective: Resolve tensions between getting things done quickly and doing them responsibly.
ethics.3.2.5.task: When a request pushes you to cut corners on a professional standard, log the conflict, your decision, and the outcome in EngineerTrack. Share with supervisor without being asked.
ethics.3.2.5.criterion: At least one such situation documented in EngineerTrack during the advanced phase. Supervisor confirms the resolution prioritised professional responsibility appropriately.

ethics.3.2.6.objective: Be open about the limits and uncertainties of your technical work.
ethics.3.2.6.task: In every technical output, add a limitations and uncertainties section. Log it in EngineerTrack naming assumptions made, data gaps, and anything that could affect reliability.
ethics.3.2.6.criterion: This section appears in every technical output in EngineerTrack. Supervisor confirms it is honest and complete. No significant risks are played down.

ethics.3.2.7.objective: Apply circular economy thinking when choosing materials or designing a process step.
ethics.3.2.7.task: When selecting materials or planning a process, complete the circular economy checklist in EngineerTrack covering reduce, reuse, recycle, and recover. Attach it to the technical output.
ethics.3.2.7.criterion: Checklist completed in EngineerTrack for at least two decisions. Supervisor confirms it is correctly applied and the choices made reduce waste or resource use.

ethics.3.2.8.objective: Stand firm on quality and safety when someone pressures you to cut corners.
ethics.3.2.8.task: If you receive a request to skip a quality or safety step, log what was asked, what you said, and the outcome in EngineerTrack. Share the record with your supervisor.
ethics.3.2.8.criterion: Every such request refused or escalated. Records clear and accurate in EngineerTrack. Supervisor confirms the response was professional and appropriate.

ethics.3.2.9.objective: Use digital or automated tools carefully and check their outputs.
ethics.3.2.9.task: Each time you use an automated or digital tool in technical work, log an entry in EngineerTrack: tool name, task it supported, how you verified the result, any limitations noticed.
ethics.3.2.9.criterion: Entry logged in EngineerTrack for every instance of automated tool use. Supervisor confirms verification steps described and intern shows awareness of limitations in at least 80% of entries.

ethics.3.2.10.objective: Write your own professional ethics code based on real internship experience.
ethics.3.2.10.task: Draft a one-page personal ethics code with at least five principles grounded in real situations from the internship. Upload it to EngineerTrack and present each principle briefly to your supervisor.
ethics.3.2.10.criterion: Ethics code has at least five principles in EngineerTrack. Each grounded in a real experience. Supervisor confirms it reflects genuine thinking rather than generic statements.

ethics.4.1.1.objective: Build and maintain a risk register that catches schedule problems before they turn into delays.
ethics.4.1.1.task: Set up a risk register in EngineerTrack for all assigned project tasks. Update it every week with new risks, probability ratings, and mitigation actions. Share with the team through the app.
ethics.4.1.1.criterion: Register updated on time every week in EngineerTrack. Supervisor confirms at least 60% of delays that actually occur were already in the register before they happened.

ethics.4.1.2.objective: Use critical path analysis to see where a project could fall behind and prevent it.
ethics.4.1.2.task: For one project task running longer than a week, map the critical path and log it in EngineerTrack. Identify float points and use them to absorb disruption without losing the final deadline.
ethics.4.1.2.criterion: Critical path and float points correctly identified in EngineerTrack. Supervisor confirms accuracy. Final deadline met despite at least one disruption absorbed using the buffer.

ethics.4.1.3.objective: Tell everyone affected by a schedule change before they have to ask.
ethics.4.1.3.task: When the schedule changes for any reason, log a brief notification in EngineerTrack and send it to all affected people within two hours of making the decision.
ethics.4.1.3.criterion: Notification sent within two hours through EngineerTrack for every schedule change. Supervisor confirms no one was surprised by a change during the expert phase.

ethics.4.1.4.objective: Work out how a delay in one task will ripple through the rest of the project.
ethics.4.1.4.task: When a delay happens, log a cascade analysis in EngineerTrack independently. List every dependent task affected, the number of days impacted, and a recovery plan.
ethics.4.1.4.criterion: Analysis in EngineerTrack correctly identifies all tasks affected directly and indirectly. Delay quantified in days for each. Supervisor rates the recovery plan as feasible.

ethics.4.1.5.objective: Prepare a backup plan for when key resources or people suddenly become unavailable.
ethics.4.1.5.task: For one major task, write a contingency schedule in EngineerTrack setting out alternative steps and resource options if something falls through. Present to supervisor before any problem arises.
ethics.4.1.5.criterion: Contingency schedule in EngineerTrack covers at least two realistic disruption scenarios with workable alternatives. Supervisor rates it feasible and detailed. Presented before any actual disruption.

ethics.4.1.6.objective: Estimate task durations more accurately by accounting for best, worst, and most likely scenarios.
ethics.4.1.6.task: For every task over two hours, log three-point estimates in EngineerTrack: optimistic, most likely, and pessimistic. At task completion, compare actual time to the range and log the outcome.
ethics.4.1.6.criterion: Three-point estimates logged in EngineerTrack for every qualifying task. Actual times fall within the estimated range in at least 85% of cases during the expert phase.

ethics.4.1.7.objective: Build environmental thinking into how you schedule project work.
ethics.4.1.7.task: When building or revising the schedule in EngineerTrack, identify at least one decision that reduces environmental impact. Log the reasoning and estimated or actual environmental benefit.
ethics.4.1.7.criterion: At least two sustainability- motivated scheduling decisions logged in EngineerTrack during the expert phase. Supervisor confirms they are logical, achievable, and show a measurable benefit.

ethics.4.1.8.objective: Help less experienced colleagues manage time and communicate delays.
ethics.4.1.8.task: Organise a 30-minute session for fellow interns on proactive schedule management. Log the session plan and attendance in EngineerTrack. Prepare a one-page reference guide and upload it to the app.
ethics.4.1.8.criterion: Session logged and delivered on time in EngineerTrack. Guide judged clear and accurate by supervisor. At least one participant confirms they found it useful, outcome logged in the app.

ethics.4.1.9.objective: Identify a weakness in how the team manages schedules and suggest a specific fix.
ethics.4.1.9.task: After a significant project phase, write a process improvement proposal in EngineerTrack: one scheduling problem observed and a specific change to fix it. Present to supervisor through the app.
ethics.4.1.9.criterion: Proposal in EngineerTrack identifies a real problem confirmed by supervisor. Fix is specific and workable. Supervisor rates it as adding value to how the team operates.

ethics.4.1.10.objective: Keep quality standards in place even when the timeline is under pressure.
ethics.4.1.10.task: When working to a tight deadline, log in EngineerTrack which quality steps you kept and any formally agreed to defer, with a reason for each deferral. Submit to supervisor through the app.
ethics.4.1.10.criterion: Record submitted in EngineerTrack for every compressed-timeline situation. Supervisor confirms no quality steps were quietly dropped. All deferrals formally agreed and documented in the app.

ethics.4.2.1.objective: Own a deliverable from start to finish without waiting to be told what to do at each step.
ethics.4.2.1.task: Take one major deliverable and manage the whole lifecycle in EngineerTrack: scope, plan, execution, quality check, and delivery. Log every key decision made along the way.
ethics.4.2.1.criterion: Deliverable handed over on time and meets quality requirements, confirmed by supervisor in EngineerTrack. Log shows the intern drove the process independently from start to finish.

ethics.4.2.2.objective: Raise ethical concerns in the team when you spot them during project work.
ethics.4.2.2.task: When you identify an ethical issue, log it in EngineerTrack and raise it professionally with the relevant colleague or in a team setting. Record what happened and the outcome.
ethics.4.2.2.criterion: At least one ethical issue raised and logged in EngineerTrack during the expert phase. Supervisor confirms it was handled professionally and the outcome documented accurately.

ethics.4.2.3.objective: Find a real sustainability problem in the team's work and do something about it.
ethics.4.2.3.task: Identify a specific inefficiency that wastes resources or energy. Log an improvement proposal in EngineerTrack. With supervisor approval, implement it and document the outcome in the app.
ethics.4.2.3.criterion: Genuine inefficiency found and addressed. Improvement documented in EngineerTrack. Supervisor rates the initiative as showing expert-level ownership and confirms the improvement is real.

ethics.4.2.4.objective: Create something useful on ethics or sustainability that the team can keep using after you leave.
ethics.4.2.4.task: Research the topic and produce a practical written resource for the team, such as a one-page ethics decision guide or sustainability checklist. Upload it to EngineerTrack and present it to the team.
ethics.4.2.4.criterion: Resource uploaded to EngineerTrack before the end of the expert phase. At least two team members confirm it is useful. Supervisor rates it as accurate, practical, and ready to use independently.

ethics.4.2.5.objective: Honestly assess your own performance on responsibility and ethics across the whole internship.
ethics.4.2.5.task: Write a self-assessment of at least two pages covering the full internship period. Upload it to EngineerTrack. Include what went well, where you fell short, and three specific professional development commitments.
ethics.4.2.5.criterion: Report uploaded to EngineerTrack on time and covers the full period with real examples. Supervisor confirms it is neither overstated nor too modest. The three commitments are specific and realistic.

ethics.4.2.6.objective: Show colleagues what can go wrong when ethical standards are ignored, using a real example.
ethics.4.2.6.task: Find one documented engineering ethics failure. Log a five-minute case-study presentation in EngineerTrack and deliver it to the team, linking the failure to long- term reputational and commercial consequences.
ethics.4.2.6.criterion: Presentation logged and delivered with at least one supervisor or team member present. Analysis of failure and consequences is accurate. Supervisor rates it as insightful and professionally delivered.

ethics.4.2.7.objective: Apply lifecycle thinking to how you design or plan a key piece of work.
ethics.4.2.7.task: For one important deliverable, map out environmental impact at each lifecycle stage in EngineerTrack: raw materials, production, use, and end of life. Log how design choices kept the total impact low.
ethics.4.2.7.criterion: Lifecycle document logged in EngineerTrack covering all four stages. Supervisor confirms the analysis is accurate and at least two design choices were genuinely shaped by lifecycle considerations.

ethics.4.2.8.objective: Notice when colleagues are acting responsibly and make sure that gets recognised.
ethics.4.2.8.task: Each week, log at least one example of a colleague showing strong professional responsibility or good sustainability practice in EngineerTrack. With supervisor approval, share anonymised highlights with the team.
ethics.4.2.8.criterion: Log maintained every week of the expert phase in EngineerTrack. Supervisor confirms examples are genuine. Anonymised sharing done at least twice and received positively by at least one person.

ethics.4.2.9.objective: Work through a difficult situation where commercial pressure and professional responsibility pull in opposite directions.
ethics.4.2.9.task: When you face a real stakeholder conflict, log a stakeholder analysis and ethical resolution proposal in EngineerTrack. Present the recommended course of action with justification grounded in ethics principles.
ethics.4.2.9.criterion: Analysis in EngineerTrack names all key stakeholders and interests correctly. Proposed resolution grounded in at least one named ethics principle. Supervisor rates reasoning as nuanced and professionally sound.

ethics.4.2.10.objective: Leave the host organisation something genuinely useful that they will still be using after you are gone.
ethics.4.2.10.task: Design and produce one lasting contribution to the organisation's ethics or sustainability practice: an updated checklist, a training activity, or a reusable framework. Upload to EngineerTrack and get supervisor sign-off.
ethics.4.2.10.criterion: Contribution uploaded to EngineerTrack and formally signed off by supervisor before the internship ends. Judged as immediately usable. Supervisor confirms it addresses a real need and required the intern's initiative to exist.

documentation.1.1.1.objective: 1.1.1. To identify the main documentation standards used in the workplace.
documentation.1.1.1.task: Review the organisation’s basic documentation rules, templates, or reporting guidelines and record at least three relevant standards in the platform log.
documentation.1.1.1.criterion: Correctly identifies at least three documentation rules or standards used by the organisation and records them clearly in the digital log.

documentation.1.1.2.objective: 1.1.2. To recognize the purpose of standard templates.
documentation.1.1.2.task: Locate one standard template used for technical reports, logs, or task records and upload an annotated blank template, outline, or short summary of its structure.
documentation.1.1.2.criterion: Explains the purpose of the selected template, identifies its main sections, and submits suitable digital evidence.

documentation.1.1.3.objective: 1.1.3. To understand basic reporting expectations for interns.
documentation.1.1.3.task: Ask the mentor which technical information must be reported during daily or weekly internship activities and upload a short reporting expectations note.
documentation.1.1.3.criterion: Correctly lists the expected reporting frequency, format, recipient, and main content to be reported.

documentation.1.1.4.objective: 1.1.4. To identify where technical documents are stored.
documentation.1.1.4.task: Navigate the shared folder, project platform, internal wiki, or document repository used by the team and submit a short note or non- confidential screenshot showing the repository type.
documentation.1.1.4.criterion: Locates the correct repository and identifies where current project documents are stored, without exposing confidential file names or contents.

documentation.1.1.5.objective: 1.1.5. To recognize the importance of document naming conventions.
documentation.1.1.5.task: Review examples of correctly named technical files and upload an anonymised list of sample file names or a short note explaining the naming pattern.
documentation.1.1.5.criterion: Describes the naming logic used, including date, project code, version, or document type, and shows understanding of its role in document retrieval.

documentation.1.1.6.objective: 1.1.6. To understand basic version control expectations.
documentation.1.1.6.task: Compare two versions of the same document and upload a redacted version label example, sample revision table, or short comparison note.
documentation.1.1.6.criterion: Correctly identifies the most recent version and explains how versioning or change labelling allows it to be recognized.

documentation.1.1.7.objective: 1.1.7. To identify required information in a technical record.
documentation.1.1.7.task: Review a completed task log, checklist, or inspection form and upload a blank form, anonymised excerpt, or platform note listing its mandatory fields.
documentation.1.1.7.criterion: Identifies key fields such as date, task, responsible person, data, result, and notes.

documentation.1.1.8.objective: 1.1.8. To recognize confidentiality or access rules for technical documents.
documentation.1.1.8.task: Review document access rules with the mentor and upload a short access- level note distinguishing between documents that can be viewed, edited, shared internally, or shared externally.
documentation.1.1.8.criterion: Correctly distinguishes between documents that can be edited, viewed only, or shared externally.

documentation.1.1.9.objective: 1.1.9. To understand the role of documentation in task traceability.
documentation.1.1.9.task: Follow one documented task from instruction to completion and upload an anonymised traceability map or short log note showing instruction, role, action taken, and result.
documentation.1.1.9.criterion: Explains how documentation shows what was done, by whom, and with which result.

documentation.1.1.10.objective: 1.1.10. To identify evidence suitable for app-based documentation.
documentation.1.1.10.task: Upload a short text note, photo, or screenshot showing one non- confidential example of documentation practice observed during the internship.
documentation.1.1.10.criterion: Uploaded evidence is relevant, clear, and linked to a real documentation practice observed in the workplace.

documentation.1.2.1.objective: 1.2.1. To identify common types of technical documentation used in engineering work.
documentation.1.2.1.task: Review project materials and record in the platform at least five document types used by the team, such as drawings, logs, reports, specifications, or checklists.
documentation.1.2.1.criterion: Correctly identifies at least five relevant types of technical documentation used in engineering work.

documentation.1.2.2.objective: 1.2.2. To recognize the function of technical drawings or diagrams.
documentation.1.2.2.task: Observe how engineers use a drawing, diagram, layout, flowchart, or schematic during a task and upload an anonymised diagram excerpt, simplified sketch, or explanatory note.
documentation.1.2.2.criterion: Explains what information the drawing or diagram provides to the project team.

documentation.1.2.3.objective: 1.2.3. To identify the purpose of specifications and datasheets.
documentation.1.2.3.task: Review one technical specification, datasheet, or product sheet and upload a public datasheet, redacted excerpt, or summary table of key parameters.
documentation.1.2.3.criterion: Identifies key information such as parameters, limits, materials, components, or operating conditions.

documentation.1.2.4.objective: 1.2.4. To recognize the role of task logs and daily records.
documentation.1.2.4.task: Review an example of a daily activity log, maintenance log, lab notebook, or project diary and upload a blank template, anonymised excerpt, or short platform note.
documentation.1.2.4.criterion: Explains how the log records completed tasks, observations, and follow-up actions.

documentation.1.2.5.objective: 1.2.5. To identify test reports and measurement records.
documentation.1.2.5.task: Review one test record, measurement sheet, or result table and upload an anonymised measurement table, sample test record, or redacted result sheet.
documentation.1.2.5.criterion: Identifies the measured variable, unit of measurement, result, and reference value or acceptance range.

documentation.1.2.6.objective: 1.2.6. To recognize quality control or inspection documents.
documentation.1.2.6.task: Observe a checklist, inspection form, validation record, or non-conformity report and upload a blank checklist, redacted form, or short note explaining its quality-control function.
documentation.1.2.6.criterion: Explains how the document supports quality control or verification of work.

documentation.1.2.7.task: Locate and review one safety instruction, risk assessment, operating procedure, or warning label and upload a public safety instruction, blank risk- assessment form, generic label photo, or short note.
documentation.1.2.7.criterion: Identifies the safety purpose of the document and one required precaution.

documentation.1.2.8.objective: 1.2.8. To recognize meeting minutes and action trackers as technical documentation.
documentation.1.2.8.task: Review technical meeting minutes or an action tracker and upload an anonymised tracker, redacted minutes excerpt, or platform note listing decisions, actions, responsible roles, and deadlines.
documentation.1.2.8.criterion: Identifies decisions, assigned actions, responsible persons or roles, and deadlines.

documentation.1.2.9.objective: 1.2.9. To identify documentation used for change tracking.
documentation.1.2.9.task: Review a change log, revision table, issue tracker, or update note and upload a sample change log, redacted revision table, or short explanation of what changed, when, and why.
documentation.1.2.9.criterion: Explains what changed, when it changed, and why the change was recorded.

documentation.1.2.10.objective: 1.2.10. To classify technical documents according to their project function.
documentation.1.2.10.task: Create an app-based classification note grouping observed documents by purpose: instruction, recording, verification, reporting, or handover.
documentation.1.2.10.criterion: Correctly classifies documents and gives one relevant non- confidential example for each selected category.

documentation.2.1.1.objective: 2.1.1. To record assigned task steps in chronological order.
documentation.2.1.1.task: Complete a supervised digital project log describing the main steps followed during one assigned task in chronological order.
documentation.2.1.1.criterion: Log entries are complete, chronological, and understandable to another team member.

documentation.2.1.2.objective: 2.1.2. To document technical results using clear and accurate data.
documentation.2.1.2.task: Record measurements, outputs, test results, or observations in the required digital format, including values, units, dates, and reference conditions.
documentation.2.1.2.criterion: Results include correct values, units, dates, and relevant reference conditions.

documentation.2.1.3.objective: 2.1.3. To use standard logbook or reporting templates correctly.
documentation.2.1.3.task: Fill in a company logbook, digital form, or task record under mentor supervision and upload the completed blank/sample template or redacted form.
documentation.2.1.3.criterion: All mandatory fields are completed according to the template requirements.

documentation.2.1.4.objective: 2.1.4. To distinguish between actions performed and results obtained.
documentation.2.1.4.task: Write one platform log entry structured into action performed, result obtained, and short comment or interpretation.
documentation.2.1.4.criterion: The entry clearly separates procedure, result, and short comment or interpretation.

documentation.2.1.5.objective: 2.1.5. To record deviations, anomalies, or unexpected issues.
documentation.2.1.5.task: Add an anonymised deviation note or issue log entry describing the expected condition, observed deviation, and relevant context.
documentation.2.1.5.criterion: The deviation is described factually, with relevant context and without unsupported conclusions.

documentation.2.1.6.objective: 2.1.6. To attach relevant evidence to support technical records.
documentation.2.1.6.task: Upload a non-confidential photo, screenshot, data extract, or short note and link it to the corresponding platform log entry.
documentation.2.1.6.criterion: Evidence is clear, relevant, properly labelled, and directly connected to the log entry.

documentation.2.1.7.objective: 2.1.7. To apply basic technical terminology in documentation.
documentation.2.1.7.task: Write a short technical note using terminology provided by the mentor or project documents, including at least five relevant technical terms.
documentation.2.1.7.criterion: Technical terms are used correctly and consistently with workplace documentation.

documentation.2.1.8.objective: 2.1.8. To update task status in a structured way.
documentation.2.1.8.task: Mark an assigned task as planned, in progress, completed, blocked, or requiring review in the platform, adding a short explanatory note.
documentation.2.1.8.criterion: Task status is accurate and supported by a short explanation or evidence.

documentation.2.1.9.objective: 2.1.9. To record supervisor instructions and follow-up actions.
documentation.2.1.9.task: Add mentor feedback, corrections, or next steps to the project log after a review, including responsible role and expected follow-up deadline.
documentation.2.1.9.criterion: Follow-up actions are clearly recorded with responsible person or role and expected deadline.

documentation.2.1.10.objective: 2.1.10. To revise technical records based on mentor feedback.
documentation.2.1.10.task: Edit one project log entry after mentor comments and upload a before/after excerpt or revision note showing the update.
documentation.2.1.10.criterion: The revised entry addresses the feedback and improves clarity, accuracy, or completeness.

documentation.2.2.1.objective: 2.2.1. To maintain a daily record of internship activities.
documentation.2.2.1.task: Complete a daily platform log summarising tasks performed, tools or methods used, results observed, and short notes.
documentation.2.2.1.criterion: Daily log is submitted on time and includes tasks, tools, results, and short notes.

documentation.2.2.2.objective: 2.2.2. To summarize completed work in a concise technical format.
documentation.2.2.2.task: Write a concise daily technical update structured into completed work, partial outputs, pending items, and next steps.
documentation.2.2.2.criterion: Entry is concise and clearly distinguishes completed work, incomplete tasks, and next steps.

documentation.2.2.3.objective: 2.2.3. To connect daily activities to the assigned technical workflow.
documentation.2.2.3.task: Tag or label each daily activity in the platform according to the relevant workflow, process step, work package, or operational area.
documentation.2.2.3.criterion: Activities are correctly linked to the relevant workflow, process, or project area.

documentation.2.2.4.objective: 2.2.4. To record tools, software, equipment, or methods used.
documentation.2.2.4.task: Add a daily log section listing tools, software, instruments, equipment, or methods used, with a short purpose for each item.
documentation.2.2.4.criterion: Record includes correct names and explains the purpose of each tool or method.

documentation.2.2.5.objective: 2.2.5. To document observations using factual language.
documentation.2.2.5.task: Write one platform observation note structured into observed fact, context, and optional interpretation where appropriate.
documentation.2.2.5.criterion: Observation is factual, specific, and clearly separated from personal interpretation.

documentation.2.2.6.objective: 2.2.6. To track open questions, uncertainties, or blockers.
documentation.2.2.6.task: Add unresolved questions, uncertainties, or blockers to the platform issue/question log, including context and requested follow-up.
documentation.2.2.6.criterion: Questions or blockers are specific and include enough context for the mentor to respond.

documentation.2.2.7.objective: 2.2.7. To organize daily evidence in a consistent format.
documentation.2.2.7.task: Upload or reference daily supporting material such as photos, diagrams, screenshots, tables, or short notes, using consistent names and dates.
documentation.2.2.7.criterion: Evidence is consistently named, dated, and linked to the correct daily activity.

documentation.2.2.8.objective: 2.2.8. To include safety, quality, or compliance notes when relevant.
documentation.2.2.8.task: Record any safety instruction, quality check, or compliance requirement encountered during the day in a short platform note.
documentation.2.2.8.criterion: Note correctly identifies the requirement and explains its relevance to the task.

documentation.2.2.9.objective: 2.2.9. To produce a concise end-of-week summary from daily records.
documentation.2.2.9.task: Review daily logs and upload a weekly platform summary including completed activities, key findings, blockers, and next steps.
documentation.2.2.9.criterion: Weekly summary is coherent, concise, and accurately reflects the daily records.

documentation.2.2.10.objective: 2.2.10. To use daily records to prepare for mentor review.
documentation.2.2.10.task: Select relevant daily entries and prepare a mentor-review note summarising progress, difficulties, and proposed next steps.
documentation.2.2.10.criterion: Intern uses records effectively to explain progress, difficulties, and planned follow-up actions.

documentation.3.1.1.objective: 3.1.1. To prepare concise technical summaries of completed work.
documentation.3.1.1.task: Write and upload an anonymised technical summary describing the objective, completed activities, and main outputs of an assigned task.
documentation.3.1.1.criterion: Summary is concise, technically accurate, and includes objective, completed work, and outputs.

documentation.3.1.2.objective: 3.1.2. To report progress against assigned tasks or project milestones.
documentation.3.1.2.task: Prepare a digital progress update structured into planned work, completed tasks, ongoing items, delays, and next actions.
documentation.3.1.2.criterion: Progress update clearly distinguishes completed work, pending items, delays, and next actions.

documentation.3.1.3.objective: 3.1.3. To present technical results using appropriate data and units.
documentation.3.1.3.task: Include measured values, calculations, tables, or test outputs in a technical progress report and upload a redacted table, calculation extract, or result summary.
documentation.3.1.3.criterion: Data are accurate, properly labelled, and include correct units and reference conditions.

documentation.3.1.4.objective: 3.1.4. To summarize technical issues or deviations objectively.
documentation.3.1.4.task: Write and upload an anonymised issue/deviation summary including observed condition, expected condition, context, and supporting note or extract.
documentation.3.1.4.criterion: Issue is described factually, with relevant context, evidence, and no unsupported assumptions.

documentation.3.1.5.objective: 3.1.5. To explain methods or procedures followed during technical work.
documentation.3.1.5.task: Document the main steps, tools, software, equipment, or procedures used to complete a task and upload a method summary, anonymised procedure excerpt, or workflow note.
documentation.3.1.5.criterion: Procedure is described clearly enough for another team member to understand the workflow.

documentation.3.1.6.objective: 3.1.6. To select relevant evidence to support technical reporting.
documentation.3.1.6.task: Attach or reference supporting evidence such as non-confidential images, redacted data tables, diagrams, or log excerpts within a report entry.
documentation.3.1.6.criterion: Evidence is relevant, correctly labelled, and directly supports the reported technical content.

documentation.3.1.7.objective: 3.1.7. To identify limitations affecting technical results.
documentation.3.1.7.task: Add a limitations note to a technical summary or report, describing constraints, assumptions, missing data, boundary conditions, or uncertainty sources.
documentation.3.1.7.criterion: Limitations are clearly identified and linked to their possible impact on the reported outcome.

documentation.3.1.8.objective: 3.1.8. To formulate practical next steps based on reported findings.
documentation.3.1.8.task: Conclude a progress report with an action list identifying follow-up checks, required decisions, responsible roles, or next technical steps.
documentation.3.1.8.criterion: Next steps are specific, realistic, and logically connected to the reported findings.

documentation.3.1.9.objective: 3.1.9. To adapt the level of detail to the report audience.
documentation.3.1.9.task: Prepare one audience-adapted technical update, or two short versions of the same update showing different levels of technical detail.
documentation.3.1.9.criterion: Report uses an appropriate level of detail, terminology, and explanation for the intended audience.

documentation.3.1.10.objective: 3.1.10. To revise a technical summary before submission.
documentation.3.1.10.task: Review and edit a technical summary before sharing it, uploading a revised version with tracked changes, a revision note, or a before/after comparison.
documentation.3.1.10.criterion: Final version is clear, complete, correctly formatted, and requires only minor corrections from the mentor.

documentation.3.2.1.objective: 3.2.1. To structure a technical report according to workplace expectations.
documentation.3.2.1.task: Prepare and upload a structured report outline or redacted report draft including required sections such as objective, method, results, discussion, and conclusion.
documentation.3.2.1.criterion: Report follows the expected structure and includes all required sections.

documentation.3.2.2.objective: 3.2.2. To define the scope and purpose of a technical report.
documentation.3.2.2.task: Write a report introduction or platform note defining purpose, context, scope, and boundaries of the technical activity.
documentation.3.2.2.criterion: Scope and purpose are clear, specific, and consistent with the assigned task.

documentation.3.2.3.objective: 3.2.3. To organize technical information in a logical sequence.
documentation.3.2.3.task: Arrange report content from background and method to results, interpretation, and follow-up actions, uploading a section map, structured outline, or redacted report excerpt.
documentation.3.2.3.criterion: Information follows a logical order and can be understood without additional verbal explanation.

documentation.3.2.4.objective: 3.2.4. To present technical information using suitable tables, figures, or diagrams.
documentation.3.2.4.task: Convert structured technical information into an anonymised table, diagram, flowchart, annotated image, or figure with clear labels and a short caption.
documentation.3.2.4.criterion: Visual element is readable, correctly labelled, and helps clarify the technical content of the report.

documentation.3.2.5.objective: 3.2.5. To represent technical data using appropriate graphs.
documentation.3.2.5.task: Create and upload an anonymised technical graph based on non- confidential, redacted, or mentor- approved data, showing trends, comparisons, distributions, tolerances, or performance results.
documentation.3.2.5.criterion: Graph is technically correct, includes clear title, axes, units, and legend where needed, and supports interpretation of the data.

documentation.3.2.6.objective: 3.2.6. To distinguish between data, interpretation, and recommendations.
documentation.3.2.6.task: Write and upload a redacted report section or platform note structured into data/results, interpretation, and recommended actions.
documentation.3.2.6.criterion: Report clearly separates observed data, analysis, and recommendations.

documentation.3.2.7.objective: 3.2.7. To reference supporting documents and sources correctly.
documentation.3.2.7.task: Prepare a reference list, document index, or report excerpt citing supporting drawings, specifications, standards, manuals, datasets, or previous reports using generic or redacted identifiers where needed.
documentation.3.2.7.criterion: References are complete enough to allow the reader to locate the supporting documents.

documentation.3.2.8.objective: 3.2.8. To ensure consistency of terminology, units, and abbreviations.
documentation.3.2.8.task: Review the report and upload a consistency checklist, edited excerpt, or terminology table showing checked terms, acronyms, symbols, and units.
documentation.3.2.8.criterion: Terminology, acronyms, symbols, and units are consistent throughout the report.

documentation.3.2.9.objective: 3.2.9. To prepare a report that supports internal review or decision-making.
documentation.3.2.9.task: Draft and upload an anonymised review-ready report summary including findings, supporting evidence, open points, and required decisions.
documentation.3.2.9.criterion: Report enables the reviewer to understand the situation, evaluate the evidence, and identify required decisions.

documentation.3.2.10.objective: 3.2.10. To submit a complete technical report with supporting annexes.
documentation.3.2.10.task: Compile and upload a complete report package with redacted or anonymised annexes, such as logs, images, calculations, tables, graphs, or data extracts.
documentation.3.2.10.criterion: Report package is complete, organized, and includes all required supporting materials.

documentation.4.1.1.objective: 4.1.1. To prepare documentation that can be reused by other team members.
documentation.4.1.1.task: Create and upload a reusable technical note, guide, or procedure. Where the full document cannot be uploaded, provide an anonymised excerpt, structure outline, or sample section with mentor confirmation of completeness.
documentation.4.1.1.criterion: Document is clear, complete, technically accurate, and usable by another team member without additional explanation.

documentation.4.1.2.objective: 4.1.2. To document technical workflows for future reference.
documentation.4.1.2.task: Create and upload a workflow map, flowchart, or process table showing steps, inputs, outputs, roles, and decision points. Where the real workflow is confidential, upload a redacted or simplified version.
documentation.4.1.2.criterion: Workflow is logically structured and accurately represents the real process followed by the team.

documentation.4.1.3.objective: 4.1.3. To produce handover documentation for an ongoing activity.
documentation.4.1.3.task: Prepare and upload a handover note including current status, completed work, open issues, risks, and next actions. Where full content is sensitive, upload a redacted version or handover checklist with mentor confirmation.
documentation.4.1.3.criterion: Handover note enables another person to continue the activity with minimal loss of information.

documentation.4.1.4.objective: 4.1.4. To consolidate project knowledge from multiple sources.
documentation.4.1.4.task: Combine information from logs, reports, meetings, datasets, drawings, or mentor feedback into a structured knowledge summary. Where source materials cannot be uploaded, provide a document index, synthesis table, or redacted summary with mentor confirmation.
documentation.4.1.4.criterion: Document integrates relevant sources coherently and avoids duplication, gaps, or contradictions.

documentation.4.1.5.objective: 4.1.5. To document lessons learned from completed technical activities.
documentation.4.1.5.task: Prepare and upload a lessons learned record including successful practices, issues encountered, and proposed improvements, using anonymised cases where needed.
documentation.4.1.5.criterion: Lessons learned are specific, technically relevant, and linked to practical improvement actions.

documentation.4.1.6.task: Propose and upload a template, checklist, or reporting structure for a recurring technical activity, using blank, anonymised, or simplified fields where needed.
documentation.4.1.6.criterion: Proposed structure is practical, easy to use, and aligned with workplace documentation needs.

documentation.4.1.7.objective: 4.1.7. To make technical documentation understandable across disciplines.
documentation.4.1.7.task: Revise a technical document for cross- disciplinary clarity and upload a before/after excerpt, redacted excerpt, or reconstructed sample with mentor confirmation.
documentation.4.1.7.criterion: Document keeps technical accuracy while reducing unnecessary jargon and clarifying essential terms.

documentation.4.1.8.objective: 4.1.8. To link documentation to supporting evidence and references.
documentation.4.1.8.task: Prepare and upload a reference list or evidence index linking the document to supporting data, drawings, calculations, standards, test records, or previous reports. Where files cannot be shared, use anonymised reference codes and mentor validation.
documentation.4.1.8.criterion: References are accurate, accessible, and allow future users to verify the documented information.

documentation.4.1.9.objective: 4.1.9. To organize documentation for long-term storage and retrieval.
documentation.4.1.9.task: Save documents in the correct repository and upload a repository screenshot, folder- structure note, or file index showing naming, tagging, storage location, and version labels. Where screenshots expose sensitive information, upload a reconstructed example or mentor validation note.
documentation.4.1.9.criterion: Documents can be easily located, identified, and retrieved by other authorised users.

documentation.4.1.10.objective: 4.1.10. To improve existing documentation based on user feedback.
documentation.4.1.10.task: Review an existing document with a mentor or colleague and upload a revised excerpt, feedback summary, before/after comparison, or change summary with mentor confirmation.
documentation.4.1.10.criterion: Revised document addresses feedback and shows measurable improvement in usability or accuracy.

documentation.4.2.1.objective: 4.2.1. To apply traceability principles to technical documentation.
documentation.4.2.1.task: Prepare and upload a traceability table, matrix, or report excerpt linking requirements, activities, results, evidence, and conclusions. Where the full matrix is confidential, upload a redacted version or simplified traceability sample with mentor confirmation.
documentation.4.2.1.criterion: Document clearly shows the connection between initial requirements, performed work, evidence, and outcomes.

documentation.4.2.2.objective: 4.2.2. To check documentation against quality requirements before submission.
documentation.4.2.2.task: Review a technical deliverable using a checklist and upload the completed quality checklist. Where the deliverable cannot be uploaded, provide the checklist, a redacted excerpt, or mentor confirmation of the checked document.
documentation.4.2.2.criterion: Deliverable meets all checklist requirements and is ready for supervisor or team review.

documentation.4.2.3.objective: 4.2.3. To maintain version control in technical deliverables.
documentation.4.2.3.task: Update a document revision table or change log and upload a revision table, change log, or version-history excerpt showing version, date, change made, reason, and author/role. Where internal history cannot be shared, upload a redacted or sample record.
documentation.4.2.3.criterion: Revision history clearly records what changed, when, why, and by whom.

documentation.4.2.4.objective: 4.2.4. To ensure consistency between technical documents and supporting data.
documentation.4.2.4.task: Cross-check reported values, tables, figures, calculations, or conclusions against source data and upload a cross- check table, verification note, or redacted comparison excerpt.
documentation.4.2.4.criterion: Reported information matches the source data and any discrepancies are corrected or explained.

documentation.4.2.5.objective: 4.2.5. To identify gaps or inconsistencies in technical documentation.
documentation.4.2.5.task: Review a document package and upload a documentation review note or issue list identifying missing information, unclear sections, duplicated content, or inconsistent terminology.
documentation.4.2.5.criterion: Identified issues are relevant, clearly described, and linked to specific sections or documents.

documentation.4.2.6.objective: 4.2.6. To prepare documentation suitable for audit or formal review.
documentation.4.2.6.task: Organize and upload an audit-ready or review-ready package including required records, approvals, evidence, and annexes. Where upload is not feasible due to file size, confidentiality, or platform limits, upload a package index, review checklist, sample excerpt, and mentor confirmation.
documentation.4.2.6.criterion: Package is complete, ordered, and allows an external reviewer to verify the documented work.

documentation.4.2.7.objective: 4.2.7. To document technical decisions and their rationale.
documentation.4.2.7.task: Write and upload a technical decision record including selected option, alternatives considered, supporting evidence, and reasons for rejection. Where alternatives or evidence are confidential, upload a redacted decision record or decision-summary template with mentor confirmation.
documentation.4.2.7.criterion: Decision record is evidence-based and clearly explains why the selected option was adopted.

documentation.4.2.8.objective: 4.2.8. To ensure compliance with applicable documentation rules.
documentation.4.2.8.task: Check a technical document against relevant procedures, project requirements, standards, or instructions and upload a compliance check note or completed review checklist. Where rules are internal or client-specific, use generic references or mentor-confirmed checklist items.
documentation.4.2.8.criterion: Document complies with applicable rules, or deviations are clearly identified and justified.

documentation.4.2.9.objective: 4.2.9. To validate final documentation with relevant stakeholders.
documentation.4.2.9.task: Submit a technical deliverable for review and upload a platform validation entry, mentor/supervisor approval note, sign-off record, anonymised validation record, or mentor confirmation note.
documentation.4.2.9.criterion: Deliverable receives approval or requires only minor corrections before acceptance.

documentation.4.2.10.objective: 4.2.10. To recommend improvements to documentation quality processes.
documentation.4.2.10.task: Propose and upload one improvement to the team’s documentation workflow, template, review process, or evidence collection method, describing the issue, suggested improvement, expected benefit, and implementation conditions.
documentation.4.2.10.criterion: Recommendation is practical, justified by observed needs, and supports better quality, traceability, or efficiency.
